﻿# Puck Workshop mod security audit — all 63 installed mods

**Audited:** 2026-10-26 · **Target:** `C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\2994020` (Puck, app 2994020)
**Result: no malware.** No token/credential grabber, stealer, ransomware, miner, RAT, persistence
mechanism, code injection or evasion was found in any of the 63 installed mods.

What the audit *did* find: one **SUSPICIOUS** item (deliberate hardware fingerprinting over plain
HTTP), fourteen mods carrying **privacy/telemetry or capability caveats**, two mods with **unverifiable
Workshop provenance**, and 46 mods that are ordinary game modding. The second previously SUSPICIOUS
item - Admin Panel - shipped a fixed build (B55, updated 2026-10-26) that was **re-audited CLEAN**;
see the re-audit log at the end.

Each mod has its own folder (`<modid>_<name>/`) containing `REPORT.md`, the full `evidence/`
(inventory + SHA-256 of every file, PE facts, API surface, raw scan hits, automated findings) and
`sources/` (decompiled C# for every managed DLL).

findings.finding: **FIXED - now CLEAN (was SUSPICIOUS).** Admin Panel's server-side handler used to execute `AdminPanelCmd` from **any** connected client and trusted a client-supplied SteamID. Build **B55** (updated 2026-10-26 22:17 UTC) resolves the sender to a server-side `Player`, authorises via `AdminLevel` / `admin_steam_ids.json` / `AdminManager`, refuses and logs non-admins, ignores the client-supplied SteamID, and blocks vote-kicks against admins. Re-audited: no malware capability before or after.

**SUSPICIOUS — deliberate machine fingerprinting.** Obfuscated `MultiAccountGuardClient.dll` (anti-multi-account guard) reads `SystemInfo.deviceUniqueIdentifier`, `steamId`, a **volume serial + enumerated module list**, and POSTs the fingerprint over **plain HTTP to a raw IP** (`http://155.212.135.111:8081/report`) plus HTTPS to `rhladminpanel.morfikgl.beget.tech` with an `X-Api-Key`. The obfuscated string table was decoded offline: no credential, wallet, keylog, screen or file-exfiltration logic exists — it is a hardware-ID ban-evasion check, not a stealer.

**Privacy — third-party uploads.** Seven community mods phone home: full **installed-mod inventory** to the game server (`3784458679`), **SteamID64 heartbeat to `puckstats.io` + cached server passwords in a local JSON** (`3497550964`), **chat lines to Google Translate** (`3822871103`), **SteamIDs to a logging backend** (`3574337071`), and **match/positional replay telemetry to `rinkpuck.com`** (`3815478693`, plus the shared `RinkApi.dll` heartbeat in `3802863574`/`3811996661`), and **SteamID64 + persona name + ranked chat text over plain HTTP to a community matchmaking IP** (`3793631096` RankUp).
**Unverifiable provenance.** Two TLAN client mods are **no longer listed** in Steam's Workshop API (`result: 9`), so author/size cannot be confirmed. Code reviewed and clean.

**Capability, not malware.** `3566470321` decrypts third-party `.abx` map bundles (AES + HMAC-SHA256) and ships base64 chat payloads — a legitimate load-and-sync design, but an arbitrary-bundle loader. `3800009738` embeds a WebView2 browser plugin plus a script that downloads uBlock Origin into the game folder and renders remote MOTD pages, so it can display anything the operator hosts.

**Everything else is ordinary modding** — game logic, stat trackers, audio packs, rink/arena/pad/puck reskins, UI tweaks. All unsigned (normal for Puck), none obfuscated, none touch credential or wallet paths.

reaudits.what: 77,824 B -> **88,064 B**, sha256 `5cd64bd1...` -> `d14311cc43942704458e245f1cd4464d4bb09b3b60fc39da840760384f98bc0b`, build **B55** (added AdminTheme, SmartBotBrain, pause/pre-game patches; **auth fix**: server-side sender + admin check, non-admins refused, client-supplied SteamID ignored, vote-kick protection for admins)
10 of 12 JPEG textures re-downloaded/re-exported (Bauer stick skins; one 154 KB -> 339 KB). No code or JSON change (reskinpack.json hash identical), no new URLs

﻿# How this audit was done — method, scoring, limitations

Audit date: **2026-10-26**. Target: every mod installed under
`C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\workshop\content\2994020` (Puck, app 2994020).

You asked for the kinds of things that actually hurt people — **token/credential grabbers,
ransomware, miners**, plus stealers, RATs, persistence and the usual Steam-account theft
patterns. That is what the checks below were built to find. No malicious code was found in
any of the 61 mods; the notable results are privacy/telemetry findings and two mods whose
Workshop listing no longer exists.

## What was checked, per mod

1. **Full file inventory + SHA-256 of every file** (`evidence/inventory.tsv`,
   `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`), so the report is tied to exact bytes.
2. **Workshop metadata** from Steam's public API (title, author SteamID64, size, subscribers,
   published date) — matched against on-disk size to confirm the installed copy is the real one.
3. **PE parsing of every executable** (`evidence/pe_info.txt`): managed vs native, x86/x64,
   .NET version, sections, overlay/appended data, entropy, signature.
4. **Decompilation of every managed DLL** to readable C# with `ilspycmd` into `sources/`, then
   read: plugin bootstrap, Harmony patches, every network call, every file/registry/process API,
   crypto/encoding, reflection, obfuscation.
5. **Pattern + string scan of every binary and text file** (`evidence/scan_hits.tsv`,
   `evidence/text_hits.txt`) for: URLs/IPs/`stratum`/`xmrig`/Monero, browser credential paths
   (`Login Data`, `WebData`, `Cookies`), wallet files (Exodus/MetaMask/`wallet.dat`),
   `GetAsyncKeyState`/`SetWindowsHookEx`/`OpenClipboard`/`BitBlt` (keylog, clipboard, screen),
   `VirtualAlloc`/`CreateRemoteThread`/`WriteProcessMemory` (injection), `Assembly.Load`/
   `FromBase64String` (packed/reflective loaders), AMSI/ETW patching, `%APPDATA%` staging,
   `CurrentVersion\Run`/scheduled tasks (persistence), AES/Rijndael decrypt loops (ransomware),
   and shell/`powershell`/`certutil`/`bitsadmin`/`vssadmin` command strings.
6. **API-surface summary per mod** (`evidence/api_surface.txt`) — a fast cross-check that the
   decompiled code and the binary agree.
7. **REA** (`open_binary` → `inspect_managed_artifact` → `inspect_managed_members` →
   `inspect_managed_native_boundaries` → `close_binary`) on every DLL for an independent
   second opinion on identity, imports/exports, P/Invoke and user strings; notes in
   `_harness/rea/`.
8. **Asset/embedded-payload checks:** bundles/PNGs/OGG/PSD checked for appended executables,
   archives or scripts (offset-based, not just "does `MZ` appear somewhere").
9. **Obfuscation handling:** where a DLL was obfuscated, its string table was decoded offline
   rather than giving up (see `3776968217_RHL_COMPANION`).

## Risk score meaning

| Score | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0–15 | **Low** — ordinary game mod behaviour; nothing that can harm the PC or account |
| 16–40 | **Moderate** — privacy-relevant telemetry, third-party uploads, or capabilities worth knowing about |
| 41–70 | **High** — invasive (hardware IDs, loaded-mod inventory, unencrypted transport) or unverifiable provenance |
| 71–100 | **Critical** — actual malware behaviour (stealer, ransomware, miner, RAT, persistence, evasion) |

Verdicts are also stated as `CLEAN` / `BENIGN / WITH CAVEATS` / `SUSPICIOUS` / `MALICIOUS`.
**No mod scored above 45, and nothing met the malware bar.**

## Limitations — please read

- **Nothing was executed.** This is a static audit. A mod could be malicious only in ways that
  require a live game/server (for example a server sending instructions no client code
  obviously implies). Server-side behaviour of every backend (`puckstats.io`, `poncepuck.net`,
  `tlanpuck.com`, `rhladminpanel…`, `155.212.135.111`) was **not** tested.
- **No native disassembler on this machine.** Ghidra/Hopper/IDA/Kuna were not configured, so
  native code (only `3800009738/native/x64/WebView.dll` here) and heavily obfuscated methods
  were reviewed via exports, strings and API surface rather than full instruction-level
  decompilation. That file is a known open-source WebView plugin, so confidence is still high.
- **Short-magic false positives.** The scanner's short signatures (`MZ`, `ZIP`, `7Z`) also match
  random byte pairs inside compressed assets (PNG/OGG/Unity bundles), which is why
  `scan_hits.tsv` shows many hits there. Only hits **at file starts** (or with a plausible
  appended-blob structure) were treated as real; the "appended payload" checks were done
  separately and found nothing.
- **Two mods are unlisted.** `3775350613` and `3778714545` no longer exist in Steam's Workshop
  API (`result: 9`), so their author, subscriber count and size cannot be confirmed. Their code
  was reviewed normally and is clean, but the *provenance* is unverifiable — flagged in each
  report.
- **One mod was unsubscribed during the audit.** `3827631915` (Shared Practice) was removed by
  Steam at ~20:56 while this run was ongoing, so it is not part of the 61 on-disk folders. Its
  earlier audit (CLEAN) is at `C:\Users\w4ua\Documents\Code\SharedPractice_REA_report.md`.
- **Signing:** every Puck mod here is unsigned (there is no signing convention in the game), so
  "unsigned" is not itself a red flag in this collection and is only mentioned for completeness.

## Mods installed after the bulk run

Two items appeared in the Workshop folder while/after the 61-mod bulk pass and were audited with
exactly the same pipeline (same harness, same decompiler, same REA pass, same report template) and
added to the table above, bringing the total to 63:

- `3793631096` **RankUp** - BENIGN WITH CAVEATS (25/100): private IP+port backend
  (`http://78.40.210.102:8787`) for its ranked/queue system, server-supplied Discord links.
- `3824708567` **APPL Cinema Studio** - BENIGN WITH CAVEATS (28/100): in-game replay studio;
  optional user-configured Discord webhook upload, clips exchanged over the game's own netcode.
  No hardcoded endpoints, no credential access.
## Re-audits after a Workshop update

A Workshop `updated` timestamp newer than a report means the DLL changed and the old verdict no
longer applies to the bytes on disk. Re-audit procedure used here:

1. hash the new file and compare with `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`;
2. copy the old audit to `_harness/_old_<modid>/` (sources, evidence, report) for diffing;
3. delete the mod's audit folder so stale decompiled files cannot linger;
4. re-run `_harness/scan.ps1 -OnlyId <modid> -Force` (fresh evidence + full decompile);
5. diff the source trees, then re-verify the previously reported finding in the new code;
6. rewrite `REPORT.md`, update the verdict table above, and log the change in the re-audit table.

# Admin Panel (3735183385) - re-audit of build B55

**Verdict: CLEAN - risk score 12/100.** Previous build (77,824 B) was `SUSPICIOUS 55/100` because
its server-side command handler accepted admin commands from *any* connected client and its admin
test trusted a client-supplied SteamID. **That hole is fixed in this build**: the server now
resolves the sender to its own `Player` object and authorises from server-side state only. No
malware capability exists, old or new.

- Mod id: `3735183385` - Workshop title **Admin Panel** (in-game admin UI for Puck, X to toggle)
- Creator: `76561199623120582` - **published 2026-05-29 22:01:38 UTC**, **updated 2026-10-26 22:17:17 UTC**
- Workshop: 1,223 subscribers, 257 views, `banned: 0`, tag `B1153 Server-sided`, reported size 88,064 B
- On disk: 1 file, `AdminPanel.dll`, **88,064 B**, sha256 `d14311cc43942704458e245f1cd4464d4bb09b3b60fc39da840760384f98bc0b`
  (inventory.tsv / hashes_sha256.txt; exact match to Workshop size)
- Internal build string: `B55` (`BuildInfo.cs`, and the startup log line `[AdminPanel] enabled B55`)
- **Changed since the first audit**: 77,824 B `5cd64bd1a826f6f63c8c9fb3fb9a44375b2cbc2666cd6c2f9400dac672720a25`
  -> 88,064 B `d14311cc...0b`. The old folder was replaced; the old copy is kept for diffing in
  `_harness\_old_3735183385\`.

## What changed

| | first audit (77,824 B) | this build (88,064 B) |
|---|---|---|
| types / source files | 11 / 12 | **17 / 18** |
| `AdminPanel.cs` | 166,857 B | 99,263 B (theme extracted) |
| `ServerCommandHandler.cs` | 32,308 B | 39,661 B (**auth added**) |
| files removed | - | `HarmonyHelpers.cs` |
| files added | - | `AdminTheme.cs` (46 KB UI theme), `SmartBotBrain.cs` (21 KB bot AI), `SmartBotBrainPatch.cs`, `PauseFreezePatch.cs`, `PauseUnfreezePatch.cs`, `PreGamePatch.cs`, `BuildInfo.cs` |
| binary string IOC scan | `MZ` only | `MZ` only (0 text hits) |

New gameplay features: custom UI theme, "smart bots" brain that replaces the default `BotBrain`,
pause/unpause puck freeze handling, a pre-game tick patch, and new admin commands
(`/spawnbots`, `/replay`, `/settime`, `/resetpuck`, `/mute`, `/unmute`, `/changeteam`, `/swap`,
`/slap`, `/jump`, `/kicksteamid`, `/bansteamid`, `/say`, `/setgoals`, `/resetscore`, ...).

## 1. Security re-check of the previous finding

**Old finding:** `AdminPanelCmd` was executed for any client; admin test trusted a client-supplied
SteamID.

**Now:**

- `OnNamedMessage(ulong senderClientId, ...)` -> `PlayerManager.GetPlayerByClientId(senderClientId)`
  -> `IsAdminPlayer(player)`. Non-admins are refused and logged:
  `"[AdminPanel] Refused a command from non-admin client " + senderClientId`.
- `IsAdminPlayer(player)` is server-side: `player.AdminLevel.Value > 0` **or**
  `CheckAdminLocal(player.SteamId.Value.ToString())`.
- `CheckAdminLocal` = the server's `admin_steam_ids.json` (dedicated server only; created as `[]`
  in `Environment.CurrentDirectory`, hot-reloaded with a `FileSystemWatcher`), else the game's own
  `AdminManager.IsSteamIdAdmin(steamId)`.
- `OnAdminCheckMessage` ignores the payload, computes the answer from `senderClientId`, and replies
  `"1"`/`"0"` to that client only.
- The client still sends its own SteamID in the `AdminPanel_Check` payload, **but the server never
  reads it** - no impersonation path. (Payload framing is validated: 0-2048 bytes, length checked.)
- Local execution exists only for `IsServer && IsHost` (the operator running the server).
- New `VoteKickPatch` blocks vote-kicks against server-admin SteamIDs and players with
  `AdminLevel > 0`.
- Client-side `RequireAdmin()` gate is UI-only; server enforcement is what counts, and it is present.

Residual client-side wrinkle (informational): `OnAdminCheckResult` does not check the message
sender, so a peer could make your panel *believe* you are admin. It grants nothing - the server
still refuses every command from a non-admin - it only makes the UI attempt them.

## 2. Capability check (nothing malicious)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Network / HTTP / C2 / telemetry | **None** - zero network APIs; the only traffic is the game's own named messages |
| Process execution / shell | **None** (the single `using System.Diagnostics;` is the default AssemblyInfo template) |
| File writes | `admin_steam_ids.json` only (create-if-missing, dedicated server) |
| Registry / persistence / autostart | **None** |
| Credential / browser / wallet / keylog / clipboard / screen | **None** |
| Obfuscation / packing / base64 blobs | **None** - readable C#, entropy 5.62, overlay 0 |
| Crypto | **None** (old "crypto" bucket hits were `AdminManager`/`SlowMotionSequence` keyword collisions) |
| Reflection | 4 uses: UI mouse-requirement check, panel font field, game `slowMotionSequence` field - normal modding |
| Harmony patches | `AddPlayer`, `Client_SendChatMessage`, `UIState.IsInteracting`, `VoteManager.Server_AddVote`, `GameManager.Server_StopTicking`/`Server_StartTicking`/`Server_SetGameState`, `BotManager.CreateBrain` |

New code (`SmartBotBrain`, `AdminTheme`, pause/pre-game patches) contains no file, network, process,
environment or registry access at all; the bot brain is deterministic in-game AI.

## 3. Residual notes (not vulnerabilities)

1. **`admin_steam_ids.json` semantics:** if the file exists and is non-empty, *only* those IDs are
   admins and the game's own AdminManager admins are **ignored**; if empty/missing it falls back to
   AdminManager. Server operators must keep it valid JSON with real SteamID64s.
2. `FileSystemWatcher` only listens for `LastWrite`; some editors save via replace/rename and may not
   hot-reload - restart the server or rewrite the file in place.
3. `ParseJsonStringArray` is a naive quote scanner: any quoted token in the file becomes an "admin
   ID". A corrupted file could produce garbage entries (fail-closed in practice, but validate it).
4. Client-side admin flag can be spoofed by a peer (`AdminPanel_Result`) - UI confusion only.
5. Unsigned DLL + Steam auto-update: this verdict is tied to hash
   `d14311cc...0b`. If the Workshop "updated" date changes again, re-run `scan.ps1` and this review.

## 4. Evidence trail

- `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt` - new DLL SHA-256
- `evidence/pe_info.txt` - PE32/i386/.NET, 3 sections, overlay 0, entropy 5.62, unsigned
- `evidence/api_surface.txt` - 17 types, 18 decompiled files, all API buckets (no Network/Process/
  Registry/Crypto/Environment/Obfuscation)
- `evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/FACTS.md`, `evidence/scan_hits.tsv`
- `sources/AdminPanel/` - full decompiled project (18 files), including `ServerCommandHandler.cs`
  (the auth fix), `AdminPanel.cs`, `AdminTheme.cs`, `SmartBotBrain.cs`, and all patches
- Old build for diffing: `_harness\_old_3735183385\` (sources, evidence, previous REPORT.md)
- Workshop metadata: `ISteamRemoteStorage/GetPublishedFileDetails` (1,223 subs, updated
  `1793053037` = 2026-10-26 22:17:17 UTC, `banned: 0`)

## 5. Bottom line

**Fixed. Safe to use on a public server again**, provided the server runs this build (B55) or newer
and `admin_steam_ids.json` (if used) contains valid SteamIDs. The previous "any client can run
admin commands" issue no longer exists: sender identity and admin status are both resolved
server-side, and the old client-supplied SteamID is ignored.

Operational advice: on a dedicated server, put your admins in `admin_steam_ids.json`; if you rely on
the game's own admin list instead, leave that file empty or delete it.

mods.report:
# RHL Companion (MultiAccountGuard) — 3776968217

**Verdict:** `SUSPICIOUS`
**Risk score:** `45/100 (Moderate)`
**Kind:** `managed .NET mod, obfuscated`
**Author:** RHL league (see `evidence/FACTS.md`) · **On-disk size:** `~0.9 MB`

## What it is
A companion client for a Russian-language Puck league ("RHL"): an in-game locker/shop for
league skins and goal effects (premium subscription upsell to `rhlpremium.ru`), plus a
`MultiAccountGuard` component that fingerprints the machine and reports which plugins/assemblies
are loaded, so the league can detect multi-accounting and patched clients.

It is not malware, but it is the most invasive mod in this collection: **hardware
fingerprinting**, **loaded-module enumeration** and **telemetry to a hard-coded raw IP over
plain HTTP**, behind **deliberate obfuscation**. That combination is why it is flagged.

## Contents
- 4 decompiled C# files, ~914 KB total. `MultiAccountGuardClient.dll` is obfuscated: every type,
  method and field is renamed to `_00A0`, `_2004`, `_2005`, … and all strings are stored in an
  XOR-encrypted blob.
- PE: i386/AnyCPU managed (.NET/Mono), **unsigned**, no overlay.
- Obfuscation: 645-entry string table in a 15,275-byte static array, decoded at runtime with
  `_4[i] = _4[i] ^ i ^ 0xAA` (see `sources/.../D6DD96C5-…cs`, static constructor). This was
  reversed offline and all 645 strings were recovered to
  `../_harness/rhl_strings_all.txt` (filtered highlights in `../_harness/rhl_strings.txt`).
- Hashes: `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`; PE facts: `evidence/pe_info.txt`; source: `sources/`.

## Code analysis
- **Identity / fingerprinting:** `GetVolumeInformation` (disk volume serial),
  `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariables()`, SteamID64 and Unity's `SystemInfo.deviceUniqueIdentifier`
  are combined into an HWID. `K32EnumProcessModulesEx` + `K32GetModuleFileNameExW` enumerate the
  modules loaded into the process (i.e. which other mods/DLLs you have).
- **Telemetry endpoints:**
  - `http://155.212.135.111:8081/report` — **plain HTTP to a hard-coded IP**, no TLS, no domain.
  - `https://rhladminpanel.morfikgl.beget.tech/puck/report-plugin` — loaded-plugin report.
  - `https://rhladminpanel.morfikgl.beget.tech/puck/report-integrity` — "Integrity report sent:
    {0} assemblies, {1} patches, {2} bytes" (client-integrity / anti-cheat snapshot).
  - `X-Api-Key` header is attached to these reports.
- **Content endpoints (normal):** `https://rhladminpanel.morfikgl.beget.tech/rhl-models/bundles/`,
  `/puck/skins?ids=…`, `/league-reskins/S7/…png`,
  `https://rhlpuck.morfikgl.beget.tech/lk/api/companion/locker?steamId=` (fetches your purchased
  skins/effects).
- **Log strings (recovered):** "Client fingerprint reporter started", "Missing SteamID or HWID —
  skipping fingerprint send", "Could not read system volume serial", "Integrity report sent",
  "Plugin report sent for …".
- **Absent:** no file encryption/ransom behaviour, no browser/wallet/credential paths, no
  keylogging or clipboard capture, no persistence (no Run key / task / service), no process
  injection, no download-and-execute of binaries (only Unity asset bundles and PNGs).

## Findings
1. **HWID fingerprint exfiltrated** (volume serial + env vars + device id + SteamID64) to the
   league's hosts. Severity: **high-privacy / moderate overall** — a persistent hardware
   identifier tied to your Steam account, held by a third party.
2. **Plain-HTTP report to a bare IP** (`http://155.212.135.111:8081/report`). Severity:
   **moderate** — anything sent there can be read or modified on-path, and the purpose of that
   host is not documented.
3. **Enumerates loaded modules and reports plugin/integrity data.** Severity: **moderate** —
   effectively an anti-cheat/telemetry agent inside your game, with visibility into every other
   mod you run.
4. **Obfuscation** (renamed symbols + XOR string table). Severity: **moderate** — no legitimate
   reason to hide strings that are just UI text, URLs and log messages; it defeats casual review.
5. **Undocumented `X-Api-Key`** shipped in the binary. Severity: **low** (key is client-side and
   therefore not a secret), but it implies a privileged server API.
6. No evidence of malware behaviour. Severity: **none**.

## Evidence trail
- Method: SHA-256, PE parsing, `ilspycmd` decompilation, REA `inspect_managed_artifact` /
  `inspect_managed_members`, plus a custom offline decoder for the XOR string table
  (`_harness/rhl_strings_all.txt`).
- Not verified: server-side handling at `155.212.135.111` and `*.beget.tech` was not tested (no
  account, and testing would mean sending real data); the obfuscated control flow was reviewed by
  strings + API surface, not by fully de-obfuscating every method.

## Bottom line
**Not malware, but treat it as an anti-cheat/telemetry client.** It reads a hardware ID and the
list of your loaded mods and sends them to the league, partly over unencrypted HTTP. Keep it only
if you actually play in that league; otherwise remove it.

# PlayerQoL — 3574337071

**Verdict:** `BENIGN / WITH CAVEATS`
**Risk score:** `34/100 (Moderate)`
**Kind:** `managed .NET mod` + asset payload (3 MP3 ping sounds, PDB symbols)
**Author:** `76561198067045734` · **Published/updated:** `2025-09-25 05:54 UTC` · **Subscribers:** `132,418` · **On-disk size:** `0.57 MB`

## What it is
A large client-side quality-of-life bundle: configurable key binds and chat macros, rich-text/markdown/kaomoji/custom-emoji chat rendering, local mute of individual players, scoreboard conveniences (copy SteamID, open Steam profile) and per-player ping/jingle sounds. Most of the code is UI and input work, but it ships a genuinely capable downloader: a user-editable `links.txt` of image URLs (seeded with default links to `files.catbox.moe`) whose images are downloaded and cached locally as chat emoji.

## Contents
- 5 files / 602,598 bytes: `PoncePlayerInput.dll` (393,216 B), 3 `.mp3` ping sounds (`PingSounds/*.mp3`, e.g. `apple-pay-sound.mp3`), and a `.pdb` debug-symbols file that should not normally be shipped to users.
- `PoncePlayerInput.dll` — managed .NET (`dotnet=1`), PE32 `machine=i386`, `signed=0`, sections `.text/.rsrc/.reloc`, overlay 0, entropy 5.66 (normal IL).
- All hashes are in `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`; PE facts in `evidence/pe_info.txt`; decompiled source in `sources/`.

## Code analysis
- 33 decompiled files, namespaces `PoncePlayerInput`, `PoncePlayerInput.PonceMods.Shared`, `PoncePlayerInput.PoncePuck.Keybinds`, `...PoncePuck.LocalMute`, `...PoncePuck.Emotes` etc. Many Harmony patches on UI/chat/gameplay-display paths (e.g. `UIChat.AddChatMessage` in `PoncePuck.Keybinds/ChatRichTextPatch.cs:9`, chat-message focus/blur patches).
- Configuration and storage:
  - `Application.persistentDataPath/PonceMods/PonceMods_ModMenuHub.json` (`PonceMods.Shared/ModMenuHub.cs:73,78`, read `:350`, write `:383`);
  - `config/ModHub/PlayerQoL/PonceKeybinds.Commands.json`, `PonceLocalMute.json` (`PoncePuck.Keybinds/KeybindRunner.cs:404-420`);
  - legacy `config/playerinput` migration (`ModHubConfig.cs:181-255`); general config read/write via `ModHubConfig.cs:305,323`.
- **Clipboard**: writes a SteamID to the system clipboard when the user picks "copy ID" on the scoreboard — `GUIUtility.systemCopyBuffer = player.steamId` at `ScoreboardUtil.cs:1612,2543,2870,3219` (logged at `:1613,2544,2871,3220`). Writes only; no clipboard reads.
- **Steam profile opening**: builds `https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/<steamid>` (`ScoreboardUtil.cs:914`) and invokes the game's URL-opener via reflection (`ScoreboardUtil.cs:4170`) — user-initiated, browser/overlay only.
- **Custom emoji image downloader** (`PoncePuck.LocalMute/CustomEmojiPack.cs`):
  - `GetEmojisDir()` → `config/ModHub/PlayerQoL/Emojis` (`:495-499`), `GetCacheDir()` → `.../EmojiCache` (`:489-493`);
  - `links.txt` is created with a header explaining the format (`:507-511`), seeded with default URL entries (`DefaultLinkEmojis`, `:46`; seeding at `:591-599`), and parsed into name→URL pairs (`:534-643`);
  - downloads via `UnityWebRequest.Get(url)` (`:693`), saved as bytes into the cache (`:703`), logged at `:721`, then loaded **only** as textures — the file scanner accepts only `.png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif` (`:451-466`) and only images are registered as emoji (`:468-471`, `RegisterFromFile`);
  - "EDIT LINKS" / "OPEN FOLDER" buttons open the local files in the OS (`:501-532`) — user action.
- Ping sounds: loaded from the mod's own MP3s through `UnityWebRequestMultimedia.GetAudioClip(fileUri, audioType)` on a local `file://` URI (`PingSoundRuntime.cs:147`).
- **Absent:** no HTTP client/`WebClient`/`Socket`/`TcpClient` (0 hits); no registry, no `Process.Start`, no `Assembly.Load`, no `DllImport`, no crypto, no base64 decoders, no keylogging (`GetAsyncKeyState`), no screen capture, no Steam auth-ticket or credential/session/cookie access, no persistence (no Run key/task/service), no auto-update or remote code execution.

## Findings
1. **Downloads files from URLs listed in a user-editable `links.txt`, with default links to `files.catbox.moe`** — `CustomEmojiPack.cs:46` (defaults), `:534-643` (parse), `:693-703` (download + write to `EmojiCache`). The downloader itself will fetch whatever URL the file lists; the saved bytes are then filtered to image extensions and only loaded as textures. Severity: medium (arbitrary remote content fetch triggered automatically on startup for seeded links; primary trust anchor is the third-party image host and the shipped default list).
2. **Ships a `.pdb` debug-symbols file** — `evidence/FACTS.md` (`.pdb=1`). Not malicious, but unnecessary information disclosure (original source paths/names) and a sign of a sloppy release build. Severity: low.
3. **Writes SteamIDs to the system clipboard** — `ScoreboardUtil.cs:1612,2543,2870,3219`. User-initiated "copy ID" action; no clipboard reading. Severity: informational.
4. **Broad chat/UI patch surface including rich text injection** — `ChatRichTextPatch.cs:9` and the markdown/kaomoji pipeline (`LocalMuteClientMod.cs:729-744` builds `<b>/<i>/<color>` markup from chat text). Rendered locally; worth noting because chat text is turned into rich-text markup, but it is the mod's advertised feature. Severity: informational.
5. **Steam profile URLs opened through the game's URL opener** — `ScoreboardUtil.cs:914,4170`. User-clicked; opens `steamcommunity.com` only. Severity: informational.
6. **No credential/token access, no persistence, no process/registry/network-socket capability** — 0 hits for the credential/persistence API set across 33 files; `evidence/api_surface.txt` shows only `[Clipboard/Input] matches=4` and `[Network] matches=5` (all `UnityWebRequest` local-file loads plus the URLs above).

## Evidence trail
- SHA-256 inventory: `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`, `evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/FACTS.md`; `evidence/api_surface.txt` (Clipboard/Input and Network categories, 33 types).
- PE facts: `evidence/pe_info.txt` (managed, unsigned, no overlay, entropy 5.66). Binary scan: 27 "magic signature" hits — mostly `MZ`/`ZIP` byte patterns inside the DLL's compressed metadata/resources and the MP3 payload; no valid embedded PE.
- Decompilation: complete `ilspycmd` output, 33 files (`sources/`); `CustomEmojiPack.cs` was read in full around the download/allow-list logic.
- Independent binary REA notes reviewed: `_harness/rea/3574337071__PoncePlayerInput.dll.md`.
- Not verified: contents of the shipped default `links.txt` URLs were not fetched (no live requests made), and the actual cached image bytes were not examined; runtime UI behaviour not executed (game not run by instruction).

## Bottom line
Keep with caveats, and consider editing `config/ModHub/PlayerQoL/Emojis/links.txt` to remove any link you do not trust — the mod downloads whatever image URLs are listed there (defaults point at a public image host) and only uses them as chat emoji, but it is still automatic fetching of remote content.

# Rink — 3811996661

**Verdict:** `BENIGN / WITH CAVEATS`
**Risk score:** `32/100 (Low)`
**Kind:** `managed .NET mod`
**Author:** `76561199623120582` · **Published/updated:** `2026-10-02 16:42 UTC` · **Subscribers:** `2045` · **On-disk size:** `20.37 MB`

## What it is

"Rink" (build B330) is a large total-conversion / league-rules mod for Puck: ~99 Harmony patches over movement, puck feel, tackling, goalies, sticks, benches/substitutions, match intro & goal presentation, scoreboard and UI, plus custom 3D models (gloves, bench, LED boards, broken sticks) and a "Rink PUG" ruleset served from the author's site. It also embeds a substantial analytics/league plumbing layer: on any server running it, the mod uploads SteamIDs, player names, playtime and stored per-player settings to `https://rinkpuck.com/api/stats`, pulls stick-skin assignments and images from the same host, shows a league scoreboard/news tab, and can auto-update itself through Steam Workshop. No credential, token, process, registry or persistence abuse exists in the code; the risk is consent and data breadth, not capability.

## Contents

- 13 files, 21,364,424 B (`evidence/inventory.tsv`).
- `Rink.dll` — 358,912 B, sha256 `bcca5a131f593ce4ba252e5aadc05418a5b739ff86b0b14be77ea03d9869c508`; PE32 (i386/AnyCPU), .NET, unsigned, 3 sections, no overlay, entropy 5.98. Managed, not obfuscated: 136 C# files, 168 types, 0 decompile failures.
- `deps\RinkApi.dll` — 11,776 B, sha256 `14d99d294e39568245eac5a3dea1f07ab3c9608e10e134b0ec8fc887c5c3346a` — **byte-identical shared component** to the one in mod 3802863574 "Arena Loader" (same author); analysed once in this report and referenced there.
- `Gloves\Glove.glb` 19,559,524 B; `Gloves\BlockerL.glb` / `BlockerR.glb` 473,284 B each; `Models\{ArenaLed 180,536; Bench 77,880; StickBrokenAttacker 4,464; StickBrokenAttackerBlade 5,680; StickBrokenGoalie 6,560; StickBrokenGoalieBlade 7,848}.glb`; `UI\rink.png` 204,480 B; `rink_client.json` 196 B (sha256 `b336a00e…`).
- The 374 "binary hits" in `evidence/scan_hits.tsv` are all inside the `.glb` files — glTF binary buffers embed PNG/JPEG and raw mesh data, so `MZ`/`ZIP`/`7Z` signatures are expected noise; keyword hits 0 (`evidence/hits_summary.txt`).

## Code analysis

**Bootstrap and patching.** `Rink.Plugin : IPuckPlugin` (`Plugin.cs:9`). The Harmony id is namespace-switched between hand-installed and Workshop copies (`com.puckcreatorrink.Rink` / `…Rink.workshop`, `Plugin.cs:27-35`). A static ctor registers an `AssemblyResolve` hook that `Assembly.LoadFile`s `deps\RinkApi.dll` (`Plugin.cs:36-47`). `OnEnable` refuses to run if another install already set `Rink.Plugin.Running` (reflection scan of loaded assemblies, `:52-58,92-131`), creates `DontDestroyOnLoad("Rink Plugin")` with `RinkBehaviour`, attaches the four network reporters (`:64-67`), applies every `[HarmonyPatch]` class via `CreateClassProcessor` (`:134-168`), and calls `RinkApi.Register("Rink","B330")`. `OnDisable` unpatches and unregisters (`:170-200`).

**Patched game methods (41 distinct targets, ~99 attribute uses).** Movement/feel: `PlayerInput.UpdateInputs`/`ClientTick`/`UpdateLookAngle`/`Server_BladeAngleInputRpc`/`Server_RaycastOriginAngleInputRpc`, `PlayerBody.FixedUpdate`/`HandleInputs`/`OnNetworkPostSpawn`/`OnCollisionEnter`/`Server_OnCollisionDeferred`/`DashLeft`/`DashRight`/extended-state setters, `PlayerLegPad.Awake`/`Update`, `VelocityLean.Awake`, `Movement.FixedUpdate`, `Puck.OnCollisionEnter`, `Stick.OnCollisionStay`, `GameManager.Server_StartSlowMotion`. Presentation/UI: `UIView.Show`/`Hide`, `UIAppearance.Initialize`, `UIScoreboard.Initialize`/`StylePlayer`, `UIPositionSelect.Update`, `PlayerHead.SetHeadgearID`, `StickMesh.SetSkinID`, `LockerRoomStick.SetSkinID`, `LockerRoomPlayer.SetLegsPadsActive`. Chat: `ChatManager.Client_SendChatMessageRpc` and `ChatManager.Server_SendChatMessage(string,string,ulong[])` (in-game command/menu plumbing). All of these are ordinary gameplay/logic patches; none hook crypto, auth, Steam ticket APIs or process APIs.

**Network — all hosts are the author's.** Every request in the mod is HTTPS to `rinkpuck.com`, plus one Cloudflare Worker used for match presets:
- `RinkApi` (`deps\RinkApi.dll`, `RinkApi.cs:69-157`): "mod_heartbeat" every ~60 s — `{api:1, kind:client|server, sid:<SteamID64>, name:<player name>, server:<MachineName|server name>, mods:{…}, time}` POSTed to `…/api/stats` with hardcoded header `x-rink-key: iZIcx2y-h29cC2GNes4SI03qtNSrK8vh` (`:29-31,144-151`). Response ignored.
- `NameReporter` (`NameReporter.cs:41,137-160`): server-only, every 60 s, POST `action:"player_join"` with each connected player's `steamId` + `name` not yet sent (`:96-133` filter: SteamID length ≥ 15, name ≤ 64 chars).
- `PlaytimeReporter` (`PlaytimeReporter.cs:79,101`): server-only, every 60 s, POST `action:"playtime_report"` with `{steamId, seconds:60}` per player.
- `SettingsReporter` (`SettingsReporter.cs:50,96-137`): server-only, every 120 s, reads `config\rink_players\*.json` (`:87-100`) and POSTs `action:"player_settings_report"` with `{steamId, updatedAt, Rink:<settings>, Puck:<settings>}` — i.e. the server's stored per-player feel/settings snapshots are uploaded to the author's backend.
- `ApiStats` (`ApiStats.cs:54-95,112-135`): **off unless the server operator puts an `ApiUrl` (and optional `ApiKey`) in `rink.json`**; then it POSTs `{ApiUrl}/api/match` with mode/level/score and per-player goals/assists/shots/saves/goalsAgainst plus SteamIDs. Used by league sites to ingest match stats.
- `StickSkinSync` (`StickSkinSync.cs:81,96-140`): every 30 s GET `…/api/stats?mode=stick_skins` (with the API-key header) → `assign` map SteamID→skin id and a `catalog` of roles.
- `CustomStickSkin` (`CustomStickSkin.cs:26,66-133`): GET `…/api/stats?mode=stickimg&id=<skinId>` → JSON `{ok, data:"data:image/…;base64,…"}` → `Convert.FromBase64String` → `ImageConversion.LoadImage(texture)` → assigned to the stick material. Image data only; nothing is written to disk or loaded as code.
- `ScoreboardTab` (`ScoreboardTab.cs:93-95,590-650`): GET `…/api/stats?mode=data` and renders teams/standings/matches/news in a UI tab; `JoinPanel` opens `https://rinkpuck.com/` via `SteamFriends.ActivateGameOverlayToWebPage` or `Application.OpenURL` (`JoinPanel.cs:11,125,129`).
- `RinkBehaviour` (`RinkBehaviour.cs:50,268-295`): when hosting and the server name starts with `RINK | PUG #` or `RINK SCRIM #`, GET `https://rinkbot.erscup910.workers.dev/preset/rink.json`, deserialise into `RinkConfig` and apply. That is a static JSON tuning preset (all fields are gameplay floats/bools, `RinkConfig.cs`), not executables or URLs.

**Server scoping.** Dedicated servers are restricted to one community IP: `IsAllowedServer` returns true only for `37.114.57.48` (the `CommunityServerIp` constant) or for non-IP/local endpoints (`RinkBehaviour.cs:49,113-135,600-637`). So the analytics uploads are gated to servers the author controls/operates, not arbitrary community servers.

**In-game networking.** `NetworkSync` defines a private named-message protocol (`"Rink_server"` / `"Rink_client"`) with 30 message types (stick break, bench, substitutions, glove holds/throws, board impact, admin request/roster/action, config chunks, client prefs) and 900-byte chunking for `RinkConfig` JSON and player prefs (`NetworkSync.cs:9-90`). It runs over the game's existing Unity Netcode connection — no sockets of its own.

**Local files.** Everything written stays under the game's `config` folder (`RinkBehaviour.ConfigFolder` = `<game dir>\config`, `RinkBehaviour.cs:76-80`): `rink.json` (tuning + optional `ApiUrl`/`ApiKey`), `presets.json` (`Presets.cs:45-47`), `rink_players\<steamid>.json` per-player settings snapshots (`PlayerPrefsStore.cs:88-116`, including deletion of its own stale records), and `rink_client.json` with a one-time `cloud_client.json` migration (`ClientPrefs.cs:27-38`). `AutoUpdate` locates its own Workshop item id, and if Steam reports it missing/outdated calls `SteamWorkshopManager.SubscribeItem`/`DownloadItem`, logging that the new build loads next launch (`AutoUpdate.cs:33-90`) — updates come through Steam, never from a URL.

**Absent.** No registry access, no process creation/shell, no `DllImport`/`Marshal`, no injection, no persistence (no Run key, task, service), no crypto/obfuscation of user data, no credential/Steam-ticket/cookie/clipboard/keyboard/screen access, no hidden downloads: every HTTP GET is consumed as JSON for UI/tuning or as a texture. `Assembly.LoadFile` appears once and only for the shipped `deps\RinkApi.dll`.

## Findings

1. **Broad, always-on telemetry to `rinkpuck.com` with a hardcoded API key, and no opt-out.** Client: SteamID64 + display name + installed-mod versions every ~60 s. Server: per-player SteamID/name joins, playtime ticks, and uploaded copies of stored per-player settings; optional per-match stats only if the operator configures `ApiUrl`. This is disproportionate for a gameplay mod and is the reason for the caveat, but it is plain HTTPS JSON to one host, the response is never acted upon, and no secrets (tickets, tokens, cookies, IPs, files) are collected. Severity: moderate (privacy/consent).
2. **Two author-controlled hosts plus one Cloudflare Worker.** `rinkpuck.com` (stats/skins/scoreboard/join link) and `rinkbot.erscup910.workers.dev/preset/rink.json` (match-preset JSON, only when hosting a `RINK | PUG #`/`RINK SCRIM #` server). Both are behaviourally limited to JSON/texture data; the workers.dev endpoint applies a fixed `RinkConfig` schema with no URLs or code fields. Severity: low.
3. **Remote images decoded in-process.** `Convert.FromBase64String` → `ImageConversion.LoadImage` → `Texture2D` (`CustomStickSkin.cs:73-120`). Parses attacker-supplied PNG bytes at worst; no file write, no code path. Severity: low.
4. **Self-update via Steam Workshop only** (`AutoUpdate.cs:33-90`): subscribes/downloads its own item through the game's Steam integration. No external binary fetch, no silent execution. Severity: informational.
5. **Heavy game-internal reflection (~37 sites) and ~99 Harmony patches**, including server-side enforcement of movement/stick values. These are anti-cheat/consistency features of a competitive-rules mod, not obfuscation or injection; patches are cleanly applied in `OnEnable` and removed in `OnDisable`. Severity: informational.
6. **Local config writes stay in `<game>\config`** (`RinkBehaviour.cs:76-80`, `Presets.cs:47`, `PlayerPrefsStore.cs:109`); `Application.OpenURL`/Steam overlay is user-initiated from the join panel. Severity: informational.
7. **Absent categories (checked against `evidence/api_surface.txt` + all 136 source files):** no registry, no process/shell, no P/Invoke/`Marshal`, no remote code load, no persistence, no user-file crypto, no credential or Steam-auth-ticket access, no input/clipboard/screen capture, no AV evasion.
8. **Shared component:** `deps\RinkApi.dll` (sha256 `14d99d29…`) is the same file shipped by mod 3802863574 "Arena Loader"; both mods therefore emit the same heartbeat. Assessed once, here.

## Evidence trail

- Method: SHA-256 inventory + PE parsing (`evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/pe_info.txt`), ilspycmd decompilation of `Rink.dll` (136 files) and `deps\RinkApi.dll` (2 files), 0 failures; pattern scan (`evidence/api_surface.txt`), Steam metadata (`evidence/FACTS.md`).
- Key files: `sources/Rink/Rink/{Plugin,RinkBehaviour,RinkConfig,ApiStats,NameReporter,PlaytimeReporter,SettingsReporter,StickSkinSync,CustomStickSkin,ScoreboardTab,JoinPanel,NetworkSync,AutoUpdate,ClientPrefs,PlayerPrefsStore,Presets}.cs`, `sources/RinkApi/Rink/RinkApi.cs`, plus the 41 patch classes.
- Not verified: `rink_client.json` payload contents (only `evidence/` + `sources/` are present, no raw Workshop payload); server-side behaviour of `rinkpuck.com`; live in-game testing. No independent REA binary note existed for this mod at review time. The 374 magic-signature hits are inside `.glb` assets (expected).

## Bottom line

Feature-rich but not malicious: it is a league-rules gameplay mod that additionally ships an always-on analytics pipeline — SteamIDs, names, playtime and stored per-player settings to `rinkpuck.com`, plus skin images and scoreboard data pulled from the same site — with no way to switch it off. Install if you trust the author's backend; block `rinkpuck.com` and `rinkbot.erscup910.workers.dev` if you don't.

mods.report:
# RINK PUGS — 3815478693

**Verdict:** `BENIGN / WITH CAVEATS`
**Risk score:** `30/100 (Low)`
**Kind:** `managed .NET mod`
**Author:** `76561199623120582` · **Published/updated:** `2026-10-07 20:43 UTC` · **Subscribers:** `15` · **On-disk size:** `0.08 MB`

## What it is

A server-side "PUG" (pick-up game) manager for Puck by the author of Rink and Arena Loader (build B14). On a server whose name starts with `RINK | PUG #<n>` it fetches that pug's roster from the author's Cloudflare Worker, enforces team and position assignment from the roster, holds the match in warm-up until the listed players are seated, and records per-player match statistics (shots, hits, saves, faceoffs, time on ice, "OVR" rating) plus a positional replay. All of that is then POSTed to the author's stats backend at `rinkpuck.com`, keyed by a hardcoded shared API key. There are 8 Harmony patches, all gameplay/statistics or roster enforcement, and no local file writes beyond a temporary `.glb` export that is read and immediately deleted.

## Contents

- 1 file, 80,384 B (`evidence/inventory.tsv`): `RinkPugs.dll`, sha256 `b3863282cee8d1fa59356298e81d066fda24bdbbdafc468f1d019e05d604af9b`.
- PE32 (i386/AnyCPU), .NET, unsigned, 3 sections (`.text/.rsrc/.reloc`), no overlay, entropy 5.93 (`evidence/pe_info.txt`). Managed, not obfuscated — 27 C# files, 28 types, 0 decompile failures.
- Scan: 1 magic-signature hit (the DLL's own `MZ` header), 0 keyword hits, no automated flags (`evidence/hits_summary.txt`, `evidence/scan_hits.tsv`).

## Code analysis

**Bootstrap.** `RinkPugs.Plugin : IPuckPlugin` (`Plugin.cs:7`), Harmony id `com.rink.pugs` (`:11`). `OnEnable` calls `Harmony.PatchAll()`, `StatsTracker.Init()`, then creates `DontDestroyOnLoad("RinkPugs")` with `StatsTickBehaviour` and `PressureBehaviour` (`:22-28`); `OnDisable` shuts the tracker down and `UnpatchSelf()` (`:38-48`).

**Harmony patches (8 targets, all benign gameplay/roster plumbing).**
`GoalNetCollider.OnCollisionEnter` postfix feeds shot-on-goal detection (`GoalNetColliderEnterPatch.cs:6-20`); `PlayerBody.Server_OnCollisionDeferred` prefix for hit detection (`PlayerBodyHitPatch.cs:8-27`); `Player.Client_RequestClaimPositionRpc` to block claiming a position outside your roster role (`PlayerClaimPositionPatch.cs:8`, uses `PugRoster.IsPositionClaimBlocked`); `Player.Client_RequestTeamRpc` to block joining the opponents' team when a roster is active (`PlayerRequestTeamPatch.cs:8,22`); `PlayerManager.RemovePlayer` to keep stats bookkeeping (`PlayerManagerRemovePlayerPatch.cs:7`); `Puck.OnCollisionEnter`/`OnCollisionExit` for shot/pass/possession events (`PuckCollisionEnterPatch.cs:7`, `PuckCollisionExitPatch.cs:7`); `PublicGameMode<PublicGameModeConfig>.OnWarmupTimedOut` prefix that re-arms warm-up while the roster is incomplete, announcing why (`WarmupHoldPatch.cs:7-35`, `StartGate.cs:27-…`). None of these touch auth, Steam, file, process or network APIs.

**Network — two author-controlled endpoints.**
1. `PugRoster.Fetch` GETs `https://rinkbot.erscup910.workers.dev/pug-roster?pug=<n>` every 60 s (15 s while no roster) and parses `{blue:[…],red:[…]}` — items may be SteamID strings or `{sid,name,role}` objects (`PugRoster.cs:12,41-146`). This is the roster used for team/position enforcement and the start gate.
2. `RinkApi.Post` POSTs JSON to `https://rinkpuck.com/api/stats` with header `x-rink-key: iZIcx2y-h29cC2GNes4SI03qtNSrK8vh` (hardcoded, `RinkApi.cs:11-13,59`). It uses a plain `System.Net.Http.HttpClient` (`:15`) off the main thread with retry backoff 3/10/30/60 s for `match_start`/`match_end`/`replay`; failure only logs a warning (`:27-52`). Every payload carries `time = DateTime.UtcNow` in ISO-8601 (`:25`).

Actions actually sent (all gated by `PugInfo.IsTrackedServer`, i.e. `NetworkManager.Singleton.IsServer` **and** server name starting `RINK | PUG #` — `PugInfo.cs:8-35`):
- `goal` — matchId, scorer SteamID + name, score, period, strength (`StatsTracker.cs:590-603`);
- `match_start` — matchId (`:1027-1034`);
- `live` — every 15 s or on phase change: matchId, period, tick, score, pressure + pressure history, and a per-player array of SteamID, username, team, goals/assists/±/shots/hits/blocks/takeaways/giveaways/posts/passes/faceoffs/time-on-ice/shifts/possession/top speed/max shot speed/hits received/saves/shots against/OVR (`StatsTracker.cs:424-427,1122-1190`, `LiveState.cs`, `LivePlayer.cs`);
- `match_end` — full `_match.Players` stats dictionary, team stats, goal list, pressure history, pug number, winning team (`:1097-1110`);
- `replay` — `ReplayRecorder.Snapshot`: matchId, 5 Hz flag, player list (`sid`, `name`, `team`, `number`) and up to 12,000 frames (0.2 s apart, ~40 min) each containing rounded position/rotation for every skater plus the puck, and `ReplayModels.Payload()` — base64 GLB exports of one skater body, one goalie body and their sticks (`ReplayRecorder.cs:118-227`, `ReplayModels.cs:34-155`).

**Local filesystem — temporary only.** `ReplayModels.Export` writes `%TEMP%\rinkpugs_replay_model.glb` via GLTFast, reads it into a base64 string, then `File.Delete`s it (`ReplayModels.cs:111,140,150`). That is the only file I/O in the mod (`evidence/api_surface.txt` `[FileSystem]` shows exactly these four lines). No other directory is created or touched.

**Absent.** No credential, session, cookie or Steam-auth-ticket access (SteamIDs and usernames are read from the game's `Player` objects and uploaded as plain identifiers); no registry; no process creation or shell; no `DllImport`/`Marshal`; no `Assembly.Load` of anything; no persistence; no crypto or file encryption of user data; no clipboard, keyboard or screen capture; no update/download of executables (the only URL serving data is a roster JSON).

## Findings

1. **Full match telemetry, including a positional replay, is uploaded to `rinkpuck.com` with a hardcoded shared key and no opt-out.** The `replay` payload is the notable one: per-0.2-second positions and rotations for every player and the puck for up to ~40 minutes, plus base64-encoded GLB models of a player and sticks. It is gameplay data generated by the server, not personal files, and it is gated to servers that opt into the `RINK | PUG #` naming convention — but any player on such a server is recorded and their SteamID/name uploaded. Severity: moderate.
2. **Roster comes from `rinkbot.erscup910.workers.dev`** (Cloudflare Worker, author-controlled) every 60 s; the parsed roster controls who may join which team, which position they may claim, and whether warm-up is held (`PugRoster.cs:12,182-268`, `StartGate.cs:27-…`). A compromised Worker could therefore gate/reject players on tracked servers but cannot execute code — the response is parsed as JSON strings only. Severity: low.
3. **Straightforward `System.Net.Http.HttpClient` with the shared static API key** (`RinkApi.cs:13,15,59-60`) and retry-with-backoff; response status is checked, body ignored. No proxy, no host switching from config, no dynamic URL construction beyond the pug number. Severity: informational.
4. **All 8 Harmony patches are statistics/enforcement hooks**, applied in `OnEnable` and removed in `OnDisable`; the only "game-blocking" behaviour is re-arming warm-up until the roster is complete (`WarmupHoldPatch.cs:15-29`). Severity: informational.
5. **Only transient file I/O**: one temp `.glb` written, read, deleted (`ReplayModels.cs:111-155`). No config, no cache, no persistence. Severity: informational.
6. **Absent categories (checked against `evidence/api_surface.txt` and all 27 decompiled files):** no registry, no process/shell execution, no P/Invoke or `Marshal`, no `Assembly.Load`/reflection-generated code, no persistence mechanism, no credential/token/cookie/keyboard/clipboard/screen access, no user-data encryption. The single `[Process]` hit is an unused `using System.Diagnostics;` in `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:1`. Severity: n/a.

## Evidence trail

- Method: SHA-256 inventory + PE parse (`evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/pe_info.txt`), ilspycmd decompilation of `RinkPugs.dll` (27/27 files, 0 failures), pattern scan (`evidence/api_surface.txt`, `evidence/scan_hits.tsv`), Steam metadata (`evidence/FACTS.md`).
- Key sources read in full: `Plugin.cs`, `RinkApi.cs`, `PugRoster.cs`, `PugInfo.cs`, `StartGate.cs`, `ReplayRecorder.cs`, `ReplayModels.cs`, `LiveState.cs`, `StatsTickBehaviour.cs`, `StatsTracker.cs` (payload sections), plus the 8 patch classes' attributes.
- Related-mod context: same author and same backend/API key as mods 3811996661 "Rink" and 3802863574 "Arena Loader"; this mod compiles its own `RinkApi` class (it does **not** ship `deps\RinkApi.dll`, despite the identical action/key convention).
- Not verified: the live behaviour of `rinkpuck.com`/the Worker, retention of uploaded replays, and the in-game effect of the roster gate. No independent REA binary note existed for this mod at review time.

## Bottom line

A PUG-organising and stats-tracking server mod, not malware: it only talks to two author-run hosts, only uploads data generated on PUG-named servers, and executes no downloaded code. Caveat: on such a server it records and uploads everything — SteamIDs, names, full stat lines and a 5 Hz positional replay of the game — with a hardcoded key and no way for players to decline.
