mods.report:
# GPM Scoreboard — 3818726796

**Verdict:** `CLEAN`

**Risk score:** `12/100 (Low)`

**Kind:** `managed .NET mod`

**Author:** `76561198936609274` · **Published/updated:** 2026-10-12 19:53 UTC · **Subscribers:** 399 · **On-disk size:** 0.53 MB

## What it is

A UI-only scoreboard replacement ("GPM Tab") for Puck that draws a Global Puck Masters league tab, a HUD, goal/announcement cards, intro/end cards, a jumbotron overlay and a shootout UI. When the current server name is recognised by the GPM website it also shows the league match context (division, round, series, team colours/logos). Toggled in-game with **F6**, off-state stored in PlayerPrefs key `gpm_tab_off`.

Everything it renders is client-side: no gameplay state is modified, no server authority is taken, and nothing about players is uploaded.

## Contents

| Path | Size | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `GpmTab.dll` | 551,424 B | The whole mod. Managed .NET (PE32, i386/AnyCPU, unsigned), 3 sections (`.text/.rsrc/.reloc`), no overlay, entropy 6.26 — the entropy comes from fonts and PNGs stored as embedded managed resources |

Single file, no folders, no native code. SHA-256 `82f51ff2a7fd1134f059de7182d884154b5e47eed4525afa3ccc15b6afcef19f`. 41 source files / 58 types decompiled, 0 decompile failures.

## Code analysis

**Bootstrap** — `Plugin.cs:7` `GpmTab.Plugin : IPuckPlugin`, plugin id `com.globalpuckmasters.tab` (`:9`), version `0.12.0` (`:11`). `OnEnable` (`:31-57`) first guards against a duplicate copy already in the process (`GameObject.Find`), then branches on `SystemInfo.graphicsDeviceType == 4` (`:36`) — on a **dedicated server** (Null graphics device) it spawns only `ServerRunner` and returns, so no UI is ever built there. On a client it creates one `Harmony("com.globalpuckmasters.tab")` instance and a `DontDestroyOnLoad` runner object (`:44-47`). `OnDisable` (`:59-86`) tears the runner down, destroys the host object, calls `UnpatchSelf()` and `Feed.Reset(true)`.

**Harmony usage** — this is the most unusual part of the mod and worth stating precisely: the assembly contains **no `[HarmonyPatch]` attributes at all**. The only patch it installs is a *read-only postfix on another mod's method*: `Feed.cs:61-100` scans `AppDomain.CurrentDomain.GetAssemblies()` for an assembly whose name contains `PuckMod_Stats`, resolves type `Codebase.NetworkCommunication` and its `static (string, string) GetData(ulong)`, then `Feed.cs:86` `harmony.Patch(methodInfo, null, new HarmonyMethod(GetDataPostfix), null, null, null)`. `GetDataPostfix` (`Feed.cs:102-115`) ignores every call except `clientId == 0` and parses the returned key/value text with regexes (`stats(SOG|SAVEPERC|BLOCK|PASS|HIT|TAKEAWAY|TURNOVER|PLUSMINUS)(\d{17})$`, `statsBATCH…`, `statsSTAR`, `statsRESETALL`, `Feed.cs:20-24`, `:117-140`) into an in-memory `PStats` dictionary. It never alters the return value and never writes back, so the only effect is "GPM tab displays extra stats when the stats mod is present". If the stats mod's reader has a different shape it logs a warning and leaves the fields empty (`Feed.cs:79-84`).

**Game reads are reflection only** — no game method is patched by GPM itself; it reads fields/properties: `UIView.View` (`BandUi.cs:83`), `UIGameState.phaseLabel`/`timeLabel` (`GameTexts.cs:27,29`), `UIView.View`+`UIAnnouncements.announcements` (`GoalUi.cs:116-118`), `UIGameState.gameState` (`HudUi.cs:243-245`), `UIScoreboard.scoreboard/nameLabel/playersLabel` (`TabUi.cs:767-779`). All read-only.

**Network** — exactly one host, and **GET-only**:
- `MatchInfo.cs:31` `Api = "https://globalpuckmasters.com/api.php"`; `MatchInfo.Fetch` (`:33-75`) does `UnityWebRequest.Get("https://globalpuckmasters.com/api.php?action=scoreboard-info&server=" + UnityWebRequest.EscapeURL(serverName))` with an 8 s timeout (`:40-45`) and parses `found/match_id/round/division/div_name/note/home/away/series` plus per-side `id/name/code/color/logo/steam_ids[]` (`:77-128`). The only data leaving the machine is **the game's own server name** in a query string — no SteamID, no player names, no session data.
- `MatchInfo.cs:130-175` `FetchLogo` downloads whatever `url` the API returned for a team logo. It only checks that the string starts with `http` (`:132`), does a second `UnityWebRequest.Get(url)` (`:137-141`), and feeds the bytes through `Assets.LoadImage` → `ImageConversion.LoadImage` (`Assets.cs:160-184`) into a 2×2 `Texture2D`. Nothing is written to disk; a non-image body simply fails to decode.

There is **no** `HttpClient`, `WebClient`, `Socket`/`TcpClient`/`UdpClient`, `Dns`, `WebRequest`, form upload or POST anywhere in the assembly (source-wide grep; `api_surface.txt` `[Network] matches=5` are the five `UnityWebRequest` lines above).

**Peer-to-peer** — game-internal only, via Unity Netcode named messages in `Sync.cs`: `"GPMTab_ask"` (`:29,:106`), `"GPMTab_sync"` (`:31,:126`), `"GPMSO_vote"` (`:114`), `"GPMSO_state"` (`:135,:302`), sent with `SendNamedMessage(..., NetworkDelivery 4)` (`:364-386`). The server answers client asks (max 5, deduped per client, `:49`) with the stats counters; shootout votes/states are relayed the same way. This is netcode traffic inside the match, not internet traffic.

**Local files** — `Assets.cs:43-139` materialises its embedded fonts (`bg600/700/800.ttf`, `pm500/600/700.ttf`, `ar900.ttf`) into `Path.Combine(Application.temporaryCachePath, "gpm-tab-0.12.0")` and rewrites a file only if the length differs; embedded PNGs are loaded straight from resources. Two debug-only writes exist: `Demo.cs:19-36` enables demo mode if `<cwd>/gpm_tab_debug.txt` exists, then `Demo.cs:144-160` can call `ScreenCapture.CaptureScreenshot(<cwd>/gpm_tab_shot.png)` and `JumboUi.cs:2102-2144` `SaveDebug` exports a jumbotron render to `<cwd>/<file>.png` — both only reachable while that debug flag file is present, and both write a PNG into the current working directory.

**Steam** — `Avatars.cs:8-79` only: `SteamManager.IsInitialized`, `SteamFriends.RequestUserInformation`, `SteamIntegrationManager.GetAvatar(steamId, AvatarSize 1)`, with a 17-character SteamID shape check and ≤20 retries 2 s apart. No auth ticket request, no `SteamUser`, no credential or session access.

**Absent categories (checked against `api_surface.txt` and all 41 source files):** no registry access; no process creation, shell or service/`schtasks`; no P/Invoke, `DllImport` or `Marshal`; no `Assembly.Load` of bytes and no dynamic code execution; no cryptography of any kind; no persistence outside PlayerPrefs; no clipboard, keyboard hook (`GetAsyncKeyState`) or screen capture outside the debug screenshot; no Steam auth-ticket or credential access; no file downloads saved to disk; no HTTP POST/upload.

## Findings

1. **Single network host, read-only.** `globalpuckmasters.com/api.php` is queried by GET with the server name only (`MatchInfo.cs:31,40`). No POST, no analytics, no SteamID — nothing personal leaves the machine.
2. **Team logos are fetched from API-supplied URLs.** `MatchInfo.cs:130-175` accepts any `http…` URL from the API response and downloads it into a texture. A hostile/compromised API response could make the client request an arbitrary URL (a request to a third party, and a way to confirm the client is running). Impact is limited to an image decode — the bytes are never written to disk and never executed.
3. **Patches another mod, not the game.** The only Harmony patch is a postfix on `PuckMod_Stats`'s `Codebase.NetworkCommunication.GetData` (`Feed.cs:86`) that observes and never modifies the result; all game access is reflection reads.
4. **All UI state is client-local.** F6 toggle in PlayerPrefs (`gpm_tab_off`), temp font cache under `Application.temporaryCachePath/gpm-tab-0.12.0`, and two debug-only PNG exports gated behind a `<cwd>/gpm_tab_debug.txt` file.
5. **Dedicated servers get no UI at all.** `Plugin.cs:36` short-circuits on the Null graphics device and runs only `Sync.Tick()` (`ServerRunner.cs:5-10`), so the tab never tries to render server-side.
6. **Automated scanner hits are benign.** The 5 binary "hits" are its own `MZ` header plus `MZ`/`ZIP`/`7Z` byte patterns inside the embedded font/PNG resources; 0 text hits, no flags.
7. **No update mechanism.** Unlike some sibling mods it never touches Steam Workshop APIs — no self-update, no subscribe/download calls.

## Evidence trail

- `evidence/FACTS.md` — 3818726796, creator 76561198936609274, published 2026-10-12 19:53 UTC, 399 subscribers, 551,424 B, 1 file, `.dll=1`, banned 0; `GpmTab.dll` PE32 i386/AnyCPU, .NET, unsigned, 3 sections, overlay 0, entropy 6.26; 58 types, 0 decompile failures; binary hits 5 / text hits 0; no automated flags.
- `evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt` — one file; `GpmTab.dll` SHA-256 `82f51ff2a7fd1134f059de7182d884154b5e47eed4525afa3ccc15b6afcef19f`.
- `evidence/api_surface.txt` — `[FileSystem] 9`, `[Harmony] 9`, `[Network] 5`, `[Process] 1`, `[Reflection] 11`, `[Screen] 1`, `[Serialization] 1`, `[Steam/Net] 1`, `[Unity] 74`; no Registry/Crypto/Obfuscation/Persistence sections. The `[Process]` line is an unused `using System.Diagnostics;` in `AssemblyInfo.cs:1`; the `[Harmony]` lines are `using HarmonyLib;` plus the single dynamic patch at `Feed.cs:86`.
- `sources/GpmTab/` — 41 `.cs` files decompiled with ilspycmd (0 failures), read in full for: `Plugin.cs`, `Runner.cs`, `ServerRunner.cs`, `MatchInfo.cs`, `Assets.cs`, `Avatars.cs`, `Sync.cs`, `Feed.cs`, `Demo.cs`, `JumboUi.cs` (debug export region), plus targeted greps of all 41 files for URLs, network APIs, Harmony calls, file IO and reflection.
- Binary REA note (independent teammate pass, `_harness/rea/3818726796__GpmTab.dll.md`): PE32, .NET, metadata v4.0.30319, assembly `GpmTab` 0.12.0.0, MVID `3c6cffff-fa48-4f4d-ab77-74b144fd8f61`, unsigned, 3 sections, 12 embedded resources (392,064 B = 7 TTF fonts + 5 PNG logos/icons) — confirming the 6.26 entropy is font/image payload, not encryption; 18 AssemblyRefs, **no ModuleRefs, no P/Invoke, no native implementations**; REA suspicion score 12/100, matching this report.
- Not verified: the shipped payload is a single DLL, so there are no external config/asset files to inspect — nothing is left unexamined.

## Bottom line

A cosmetic league scoreboard. It phones exactly one website (`globalpuckmasters.com`) with a plain GET containing the server name, downloads team logos from URLs that site hands back, and otherwise only reads game UI state by reflection and talks to the match over Netcode. No credentials, no persistence, no code loading, no uploads. The only thing to keep in mind is that it will make a network request to whatever logo URL the league API names — harmless as an image decode, but not something you'd want on an air-gapped box. Safe to install.

# Sounds — 3574183948

**Verdict:** `CLEAN`
**Risk score:** `12/100 (Low)`
**Kind:** `managed .NET mod` (audio playback framework / server-authoritative sound cues)
**Author:** `76561198025378067` · **Published/updated:** `2025-09-24 21:38 UTC` · **Subscribers:** `133,997` · **On-disk size:** `0.09 MB`

## What it is
The sound engine that other "sounds pack" mods plug into: goal horns, goal music, period/warmup/game-over music, faceoff and chat-triggered sounds. It discovers `.ogg` files shipped by sound-pack mods, loads them as Unity `AudioClip`s, plays them synchronised for all players from the server, and stores per-pack and per-user settings. It reads a local donor-preferences file (SteamID → chosen goal song/horn), but nothing is sent anywhere outside the game session.

## Contents
- 1 file / 89,600 bytes: only `oomtm450PuckMod_Sounds.dll`.
- `oomtm450PuckMod_Sounds.dll` — 89,600 B, managed .NET (`dotnet=1`), PE32 `machine=i386`, `signed=0`, sections `.text/.rsrc/.reloc`, overlay 0, entropy 5.84 (normal IL).
- All hashes are in `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`; PE facts in `evidence/pe_info.txt`; decompiled source in `sources/`.

## Code analysis
- 30 decompiled files, namespaces `oomtm450PuckMod_Sounds`, `...Configs`, `Codebase`. Harmony patches: `BaseGameMode.OnGameStateChanged` (`Sounds.cs:17`), `StandardGameMode.OnPreGameTimedOut` (`:154`), `BaseGameMode.ScoreGoal` (`:181`), `SynchronizedAudio.Server_PlayRpc` (`:216`, intercepts game audio RPC so mod audio plays with the game's own sound sync), `ChatManager.Client_SendChatMessage` (`:249`, chat commands), `PhysicsManager.Update` (`:465`, client tick).
- Audio loading: `SoundsSystem.cs:639` enumerates `*.ogg` under a sound-pack folder, `:648-651` reads the pack's `settings.json`, `:767` writes it back; clips are loaded through `SoundsSystem.cs:313` (`WebRequestAudioClipAsync(..., new Uri(value.FilePath), ...)`) — a `file://` URI into the pack's own folder, i.e. local disk, not a network fetch.
- Playback orchestration: server broadcasts `playsound`/`stopsound` named messages with the sound identifier (`Sounds.cs:61,67,72,78,79,84,85,90,114,202,206,790,793,796,1018,1021,1022,1344,1354,1361`); the receiver validates and plays. Interop with sound packs uses `loadextrasounds` (`:1018`) and a version exchange (`:1012,1027`).
- Filesystem:
  - donor preferences read: `config/poncepuck_user_data.json` — `DonorPrefs.cs:25` (path), `:69` (`File.ReadAllText` → `JsonConvert.DeserializeObject<UserDataDto>`), containing `GoalSongs`/`GoalHorns` dictionaries keyed by SteamID (`DonorPrefs.cs:12-17`); cached in memory and refreshed on file mtime change (`:55-75`). Read-only, local, never transmitted.
  - own configs: `config/oomtm450_sounds_clientconfig.json` and `..._serverconfig.json` (standard config read/write in `ClientConfig.cs` / `ServerConfig.cs`).
  - per-pack `settings.json` inside each sound-pack folder (`SoundsSystem.cs:648,651,767`).
- **Absent:** no external network APIs (`HttpClient`/`WebClient`/`Socket`/`TcpClient` — 0 hits across 30 files), no registry, no `Process.Start`, no `Assembly.Load`, no `DllImport`, no crypto, no base64, no clipboard, no screen capture, no Steam auth-ticket or credential access, no persistence.

## Findings
1. **Six Harmony patches, including `SynchronizedAudio.Server_PlayRpc`** — `Sounds.cs:17,154,181,216,249,465`. The audio-RPC patch is how mod sounds join the game's own synchronised audio playback; no host-level effect. Severity: informational.
2. **Reads `config/poncepuck_user_data.json` mapping SteamIDs to chosen goal songs/horns** — `DonorPrefs.cs:25,69`. Local read of a server file used for donor perks; the data is not sent off-machine and is not credentials (no tokens/session/cookies). Severity: informational.
3. **`UnityWebRequestAudioClip` used on `file://` URIs** — `SoundsSystem.cs:313`. Scans for "WebRequest" flag this, but the target is the mod's own local `.ogg` file. Severity: informational.
4. **Writes `settings.json` into sound-pack folders under the game's `Plugins`/mod dirs** — `SoundsSystem.cs:767`. Only the pack's own volume/settings metadata. Severity: informational.
5. **No external communication or host-level API use** — 0 risky-API hits across 30 files; `evidence/api_surface.txt` `[Network] matches=25` are all Netcode/`NetworkCommunication` symbols.

## Evidence trail
- SHA-256 inventory: `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`, `evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/FACTS.md`.
- PE facts: `evidence/pe_info.txt` (managed, unsigned, no overlay, entropy 5.84). Binary scan: 1 hit (`MZ` header at 0).
- Decompilation: complete `ilspycmd` output, 30 files (`sources/`).
- Independent binary REA notes reviewed: `_harness/rea/3574183948__oomtm450PuckMod_Sounds.dll.md`.
- Not verified: actual playback timing/sync in a live match (game not run by instruction); content of a real `poncepuck_user_data.json` (only its parsed shape is known).

## Bottom line
Keep. It is the audio engine for sound packs: it loads local `.ogg` files, plays them on the server's cue, and reads/writes only its own JSON settings — no internet, no OS-level access.

# Shootouts — 3630067097

**Verdict:** `CLEAN`
**Risk score:** `9/100 (Low)`
**Kind:** `managed .NET mod`
**Author:** `76561198057883682` · **Published/updated:** `2025-12-24 02:51 UTC` · **Subscribers:** `91,931` · **On-disk size:** `0.67 MB`

## What it is

A penalty-shootout / mini-game mode for Puck. It takes over the game state machine, positions shooters and goalies, scores individual attempts, runs an order-vote system, and draws its own HUD and menus. It ships a config example pair, a banner image and a whistle sound effect alongside the DLL.

The DLL is required; the `.json` files are example configs for server owners, and the `.wav`/`.png` are cosmetic.

## Contents

- 6 files / 0.67 MB (no folders): `ShootoutMod.dll` (198,144 B), `preview.png` (366,922 B), `Whistle.wav` (131,278 B), `shootout_config_EXAMPLE.json` (935 B), `server_configuration_EXAMPLE.json` (907 B), `readme` (102 B, no extension).
- DLL: `ShootoutMod.dll`, 198,144 B, sha256 `145543f5783d6ee646c667b537b2a7b7c7a34929b43ec9e2e5398f98c4e235fd`, **managed .NET** (dotnet=1), **unsigned**, PE32 i386, subsystem CUI, 3 sections (`.text/.rsrc/.reloc`), overlay 0, entropy 5.75 — normal compiled .NET assembly, **not obfuscated** (29 source files / 37 types, readable C# with real names).
- All hashes are in `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`; PE facts in `evidence/pe_info.txt`; decompiled source in `sources/`.

## Code analysis

**Bootstrap.** `PoncePuck.Shootout/ShootoutPlugin.cs` + `ShootoutMod.cs` implement `IPuckPlugin`; `OnEnable()` creates a `Harmony`, patches, and initialises a UI game object; `OnDisable()` unpatches and tears down. On a dedicated server (`Application.isBatchMode`) the UI paths are skipped (`ShootoutMod.cs:75`, `:81`, `:87`, `:128`).

**Harmony patches — 5 game methods.** `Puck_OnCollisionEnter_Patch.cs:7` (`Puck.OnCollisionEnter`), `BaseGameMode_ScoreGoal_Patch.cs:9` (`[HarmonyPatch]` / target resolved by attribute arguments), `ShootoutMod_GameManager_Server_SetGameState_Patch.cs:9` (`GameManager.Server_SetGameState`), `ShootoutMod_UIScoreboard_AddPlayer_Patch.cs:9` (`UIScoreboard.AddPlayer`), `CustomCommandUnknownCommandPatch.cs:8` (the game's unknown-slash-command handler, to add mod commands). These are the mechanism by which the mod runs its own game phase — expected for a game-mode mod, and they only alter game state, not OS behaviour.

**Network — two netcode surfaces, both narrow and both already present in the game's session.**
- Server side (`ShootoutMod_NetworkHandlers.cs:14 HandleClientMessage`) accepts exactly three client messages: `"ShootoutModAskStartupData"`, `"ShootoutModAskShootoutState"`, and `"ShootoutModSubmitOrderVote"` (an index array clamped to 0–32 at `:36–:43` before use). **There is no client command-execution channel**: no arbitrary command strings are accepted from clients, no admin actions are triggered remotely.
- Client side (`HandleServerMessage` at `:60`) parses `"ShootoutModStartupData"` (version string, warns on mismatch with `3.0.0`) and `"ShootoutModShootoutState"` (a `Dictionary<string,object>` from JSON that only drives the mod's own HUD, `:80–:88`).
- There is **no `HttpClient`, `WebClient`, `WebRequest`, `Socket`, `TcpClient`, `UdpClient` or Steam API call anywhere**. The only `UnityWebRequest` in the mod is `ShootoutUI.cs:1647 UnityWebRequestMultimedia.GetAudioClip("file:///" + filePath, AudioType 20)` — a **local file** audio loader for `Whistle.wav`, not a network request.
- The only external URL is `ShootoutSettingsUI.cs:427 Application.OpenURL("https://buymeacoffee.com/amikiir")` (the author's tip jar button, user-clicked). No data is sent with it.

**Admin authority is delegated to the game, not invented.** `AdminRegistry.cs:38 IsAdminSteamId(string)` and `:70 IsAdminPlayer(Player)` resolve admin status through the game's own `AdminManager.IsSteamIdAdmin(...)` (`:53`) after normalising the SteamID. `ShootoutController.cs:4335/4340/4349` uses that. So a client cannot promote itself; whatever the server's real admin list says, applies.

**Filesystem — two config files, plus one shared menu registry.**
- Server config: `ShootoutConfigManager.cs:44–:51` → `<server root>/config/shootout_config.json`; read `:98`, written `:117`.
- Client config: `ShootoutConfigManager.cs:54–:88` → `<game root>/config/ModHub/shootout_client_config.json`; read `:132`.
- Shared PonceMods menu registry: `PonceMods.Shared/ModMenuHub.cs:83–:88` → `Application.persistentDataPath/PonceMods/PonceMods_ModMenuHub.json`, read `:361 File.ReadAllLines`, written `:394 File.WriteAllLines`, deleted `:429 File.Delete` when empty. This is a local registry of installed Ponce-family mods so they can share one menu button.
- Every path above is inside the game's own tree or Unity's persistent data folder. Nothing touches Documents, Desktop, browser profiles, or other applications' data.

**Reflection — used only to find sibling mods' menus.** `ModMenuHub.cs:177` reads `_localCallbacks` via non-public reflection, `:209`/`:268` read `_localRunner`, `:217`/`:276` read the `IsPrimary` property, `:221` invokes `OpenModPanelPublic`. `MaxPractice`/`CompetitiveAdjustments` (same author family) contain the matching `PonceMods.Shared.ModMenuHub` type, which is what this is looking for. Read-only access to private fields of a known type; no code generation, no dynamic assembly loading.

**Absent categories (checked against `evidence/api_surface.txt` and all 29 sources).** No HTTP/network client, no socket, no URL upload, no Steam API call. **No Windows registry access** — the three `[Registry]` lines in `api_surface.txt` are `ShootoutController.cs:4335/4340/4349` referencing the mod's *own* class `AdminRegistry`, which is a SteamID allow-list wrapper, not `Microsoft.Win32`. No crypto (`Aes`/`Rijndael`/`CryptoStream`) — the `[Crypto]` category is absent — and no base64. No `Assembly.Load`/`LoadFrom`/`Emit`. No P/Invoke, no `DllImport`, no `Marshal`. No input capture, no clipboard, no screen capture. No credential/token/session access (`GetAuthTicket` absent). No persistence (no Run key, no scheduled task, no service). No AV/AMSI/ETW evasion, no obfuscation, no anti-debug. `ShootoutController.cs:547 new Random(Environment.TickCount ^ (int)DateTime.UtcNow.Ticks)` is a gameplay RNG seed, not cryptography.

## Findings

1. **Client→server message surface is three whitelisted messages, none of which executes commands** (`ShootoutMod_NetworkHandlers.cs:24–:52`). The only client-controlled input reaching server logic is a vote array that is range-clamped before use (`:36–:43`). Good design; nothing to exploit for privilege escalation. **Severity: informational (positive).**
2. **Opens the author's tip-jar page in the default browser on click** (`ShootoutSettingsUI.cs:427`, `https://buymeacoffee.com/amikiir`). No query parameters, no data attached. **Severity: low.**
3. **Loads `Whistle.wav` through `UnityWebRequestMultimedia`** (`ShootoutUI.cs:1647`, `"file:///" + filePath`). Looks like a network call in a keyword scan but is a local `file://` URI with no host component. **Severity: informational.**
4. **34 automated "magic signature" hits are false positives.** 16 are `MZ`/`ZIP`/`7Z` byte sequences at scattered offsets inside `preview.png` (offset 51173 `MZ`, 108583 `ZIP`, 161014 `7Z`, …, 343350 `7Z` — normal for compressed PNG data), one is `ShootoutMod.dll 0 MZ` (the DLL's own header), and one is a raw `https://` ASCII run at offset 75 inside `Whistle.wav` (audio sample bytes that happen to spell it; no code reads it). `hits_summary.txt`: `keyword hits: 0`, zero text-pattern hits. **Severity: informational (scan artefact).**
5. **Writes a shared mod-menu JSON in Unity's persistent data path** (`ModMenuHub.cs:83–:88`) and reads it back. It records installed Ponce mods/menu entries; no user or account data. **Severity: low.**
6. **Five Harmony patches on core game methods**, including `GameManager.Server_SetGameState` and `UIScoreboard.AddPlayer`. Necessary for a custom game mode; means the mod must be installed on both server and clients for consistent behaviour, and can break after a game patch. **Severity: informational.**

## Evidence trail

- Method: SHA-256 inventory of all 6 files (`evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`), PE header parsing (`evidence/pe_info.txt`), `ilspycmd` decompilation of `ShootoutMod.dll` into 29 C# files across 4 namespaces (`sources/ShootoutMod/`), automated signature/keyword scan (`evidence/scan_hits.tsv`, `hits_summary.txt`), full source review plus `api_surface.txt` cross-check.
- Read in full: `ShootoutMod_NetworkHandlers.cs`, `AdminRegistry.cs`, `ShootoutConfigManager.cs`, `PonceMods.Shared/ModMenuHub.cs`, and the five Harmony patch classes.
- Keyword roll-up across every `.cs`: `HttpClient`/`WebClient`/`Socket`/`http` — none; `Registry` (Windows) — none (only the mod's own `AdminRegistry` class); `Assembly.Load` — none; `FromBase64String` — none; `GetAuthTicket` — none; `Clipboard` — none; `GetAsyncKeyState` — none; `DllImport`/`Marshal.` — none; `Aes`/`Rijndael`/`CryptoStream` — none; `DownloadFile`/`DownloadString` — none; `Steamworks` — none; `powershell`/`schtasks`/`RunKey` — none. All `File.*` and `Application.OpenURL` hits are the lines cited above.
- What could NOT be verified: runtime behaviour on a live server was not executed (game not run); the vote-aggregation and score logic were read statically only. The `readme` file (102 B) was not quoted; `preview.png` and `Whistle.wav` were hashed and scanned but not rendered/played. No REA binary note exists for this DLL.

## Bottom line

Keep. A well-behaved game-mode mod: its client-facing netcode accepts three fixed message types and no commands, admin checks go through the game's own admin list, it writes two JSON configs and one local menu registry, and it has no network client, no registry access, no crypto, no persistence and no download capability. The tip-jar link and the whistle sound are the only external-looking things, and both are inert.

1. **Three Harmony patches on stick/puck sound trigger points** — `GameSoundPatches_Workshop.cs:44,87,160`. Exactly the advertised feature (custom impact sounds); no gameplay-authority or host-level effect. Severity: informational.

3. **`http://` strings inside `preview.png`** — `evidence/FACTS.md` binary hits. Image metadata text chunks in the Workshop preview art; no code path references the PNG. Severity: informational.
4. **No network/registry/process/crypto capability** — 0 risky-API hits across the 5 source files; `evidence/api_surface.txt` shows no network category except the local-media load.

## Evidence trail
- SHA-256 inventory: `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`, `evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/FACTS.md` (24 files, 21 `.wav`).
- PE facts: `evidence/pe_info.txt` (managed, unsigned, no overlay, entropy 5.48). Binary scan: `evidence/scan_hits.tsv` (104 hits in WAV/PNG payloads, explained above).
- Decompilation: complete `ilspycmd` output, 5 files (`sources/`); all five files are short and were read in full.
- No independent REA binary note exists for this DLL (`_harness/rea/` has none for 3724352946) — conclusions rest on decompiled source + PE facts, so confidence in "no hidden native code" is slightly reduced (though PE facts show no native sections/overlay).
- Not verified: sound replacement behaviour in a live game (not run by instruction); the 21 WAVs were not decoded, treated as media by extension/magic/absence of loader logic.

## Bottom line
Keep. It hooks three in-game sound triggers and plays its own local WAV files; the `http://` hits are text inside the preview image, and there is no networking or OS-level access.

# Replay — 3612637610

**Verdict:** `CLEAN`
**Risk score:** `8/100 (Low)`
**Kind:** `managed .NET mod`
**Author:** `76561198132874833` · **Published/updated:** `2025-11-26 10:20 UTC` · **Subscribers:** `1,303` · **On-disk size:** `0.16 MB`

## What it is

A replay recorder and player for Puck. It records a match into a compact custom binary file (`.prp`), then lets you browse, play back and delete recordings from an in-game menu — re-spawning players, sticks and the puck from the recorded event stream while a separate camera follows the action.

The DLL is the entire mod; there are no assets, no native code, no scripts.

## Contents

- 1 file / 0.16 MB: `Replay.dll`.
- DLL: `Replay.dll`, 164,352 B, sha256 `ba4fae02684fc5839b04af03f85bc8793a159ebccce9d5cea97f621e38734d07`, **managed .NET** (dotnet=1), **unsigned**, PE32 i386, subsystem CUI, 3 sections (`.text/.rsrc/.reloc`), overlay 0, entropy 5.74 — normal for a compiled .NET assembly, **not obfuscated** (67 source files / 75 types decompile to readable C# with real member names).
- All hashes are in `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`; PE facts in `evidence/pe_info.txt`; decompiled source in `sources/`.

## Code analysis

**Bootstrap.** `Replay/ReplayMod/Plugin.cs` implements `IPuckPlugin`; `OnEnable()` instantiates a `Harmony` and calls `PatchAll()`, `OnDisable()` calls `UnpatchSelf()`. Recording and playback are driven through `CustomReplayRecorder`, `CustomReplayPlayer`, `CustomReplayManager` and `AdvancedReplayEngine`.

**Harmony patches — 9, all read-only or protective.** `PatchCursorDuringReplay.cs:6` (`UIManager.CheckMouseRequirement`), `PatchDisableScoreboardUpdates.cs:10` and `:34` (`UIScoreboard.AddPlayer` / `RemovePlayer`), `PatchProtectPuckSpawning.cs:9` and `:33` (`PuckManager.Server_SpawnPucksForPhase` / `Server_SpawnPuck`), `PatchProtectReplayStop.cs:9` and `:32` (`ReplayPlayer.Server_StopReplay` / `ReplayRecorder.Server_StopRecording`), `PatchReplayCameraFollow.cs:11` (`ReplayCamera.OnTick`), `PatchStickPhysicsDuringReplay.cs:7` (`Stick.FixedUpdate`), `UIChat_AddChatMessage_Patch.cs:7` (`UIChat.AddChatMessage`). Their purpose is to stop the game from tearing down replay state or spawning extra pucks while a replay is being scrubbed — they suppress game actions, they do not add any outbound behaviour.

**Network — no network APIs of any kind.** There is no `HttpClient`, `WebClient`, `WebRequest`, `UnityWebRequest`, `Socket`, `TcpClient`, `UdpClient`, named pipe or Steam API call in any of the 67 source files; `evidence/api_surface.txt` has **no `[Network]` section at all** for this mod. Replay data is stored and played back entirely on the local machine. No URL, hostname or port appears in the code.

**Filesystem — contained and predictable.**
- Replay files: `ReplayBinarySerializer.cs:95 File.WriteAllBytes(filePath, array)`, read back at `:113 File.ReadAllBytes(filePath)` / `:154 FileStream(filePath, FileMode.Open, FileAccess.Read)`.
- Location: `CleanStorageHelper.cs:21–:26` → `Application.persistentDataPath/Replays` on a client, or `<server root>/Replays` on a dedicated server; `*.prp` only.
- Retention: `CleanStorageHelper.CleanStorage(int limitMB)` lists `*.prp` in *that* folder only, and when the total exceeds the user's configured limit deletes the **oldest** files until it is under budget (`ClearStorageHelper.cs:34 Directory.GetFiles(empty, "*.prp", SearchOption.TopDirectoryOnly)`).
- Manual delete: `ReplayMenu.cs:704 File.Delete(replay.FilePath)` — only the selected replay.
- Settings: `ModSettings.cs:74–:77` → `<game>/config/<ConfigurationFileName>`, JSON via `System.Text.Json` (`:38 Deserialize`, `:51`/`:68 File.WriteAllText`).
- Nothing is written to Documents, Desktop, AppData, temp, or outside the two paths above.

**Serialization is hand-rolled, not dangerous.** `ReplayBinarySerializer` is a bespoke format: a magic int `1347571712` and version `3` (`:216–:217`), then per-event `tick`/type-byte/length-prefixed payload, dispatched by an explicit `switch` on the known event-type name (`:583`). There is **no `BinaryFormatter`, no `SoapFormatter`, no type-name-driven `Type.GetType` deserialization, no `XmlSerializer` of attacker-chosen types** — i.e. none of the classic .NET deserialization-RCE patterns. Bounded reads: strings are `ushort`-length-prefixed (`ReadStr` at `:1006–:1009`) and event payloads are `ushort`-length-prefixed (`:557–:558`), so a crafted `.prp` cannot request a multi-GB allocation through those fields.

**Process execution — two fixed, benign uses, both user-clicked.**
1. `ReplayMenu.cs:618` `Process.Start("https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/" + replayHeader.RecorderSteamId)` — clicking the recorder's name opens their Steam profile in the default browser. The string is hard-prefixed with the `https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/` URL, so the shell handler treats it as a URL, not a file.
2. `ReplayMenu.cs:679–:684` `Process.Start(new ProcessStartInfo { FileName = "explorer.exe", Arguments = "/select,\"" + fullPath + "\"", UseShellExecute = true })` — the "Open containing folder" context-menu item.

**Reflection — 4 private-field reads, all game types.** `AdvancedReplayEngine.cs:667 typeof(UIChat).GetField("chatMessageAsset", Instance|NonPublic)`; `PatchStickPhysicsDuringReplay.cs:10`/`:12 typeof(Stick).GetField("rotationContainer"/"bladeAngleStep", NonPublic)`; `ReplayMenuAccessButtons.cs:14 typeof(UIMainMenu).GetField("settingsButton", NonPublic)`. These are read-only UI/physics handles required by the replay rendering; nothing is written and no code is generated.

**Absent categories (checked against `evidence/api_surface.txt` and all 67 sources).** No network APIs of any kind. **No registry access** (no `[Registry]` category, no `RegistryKey`/`Microsoft.Win32` anywhere). No crypto (`Aes`/`Rijndael`/`CryptoStream`) and no base64. No `Assembly.Load`/`Assembly.LoadFrom`/`Emit`/dynamic code loading. No P/Invoke, no `DllImport`, no `Marshal`. No input capture (`GetAsyncKeyState`, clipboard), no screen capture. No credential, token, session or cookie access — `GetAuthTicket` never appears. No Steamworks API. No persistence (no Run key, no scheduled task, no service, no startup entry). No AV/AMSI/ETW evasion, no obfuscation, no anti-debug, no environment fingerprinting.

## Findings

1. **Launches the default browser with a Steam profile URL built from replay metadata** (`ReplayMenu.cs:618`). Only reachable by clicking the recorder's name in the replay list; the URL prefix is hard-coded so the target host cannot be redirected to an arbitrary file or site. **Severity: low.**
2. **Launches `explorer.exe /select,"<path>"`** (`ReplayMenu.cs:679–:684`) for "Open containing folder". Standard shell invocation, path comes from the mod's own replay list (`Path.GetFullPath(replay.FilePath)`). **Severity: low.**
3. **Automatic deletion of old replay files** (`CleanStorageHelper.cs`, `CleanStorage(int limitMB)`). When the user-configured size limit is exceeded, the oldest `.prp` files in the `Replays` folder are deleted without further prompting. It is strictly scoped — `SearchOption.TopDirectoryOnly`, `"*.prp"` glob, only its own folder — but a user who expects recordings to persist should know. **Severity: low (by design, user-configurable).**
4. **Nine Harmony patches on game methods** including `UIScoreboard.AddPlayer`/`RemovePlayer` and `Stick.FixedUpdate`. Replay support genuinely requires suppressing live-game state updates while scrubbing; the patches only skip game calls. This is the normal cost of this kind of mod, and the reason a replay mod must be installed by everyone in the lobby for a match to look identical. **Severity: informational.**
5. **Unsigned, private-field reflection into `UIChat`/`Stick`/`UIMainMenu`** (`AdvancedReplayEngine.cs:667`, `PatchStickPhysicsDuringReplay.cs:10`/`:12`, `ReplayMenuAccessButtons.cs:14`). Fragile across game builds (the mod breaks rather than misbehaves on a version bump), but not a security issue. **Severity: informational.**

## Evidence trail

- Method: SHA-256 inventory (`evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`), PE header parsing (`evidence/pe_info.txt`), `ilspycmd` decompilation of the single managed DLL into 67 C# files (`sources/Replay/`), automated magic-signature/keyword scan (`evidence/scan_hits.tsv` — 1 hit: the `MZ` at offset 0 of the DLL itself; `hits_summary.txt` — 0 magic, 0 keyword), full-source pattern review plus `api_surface.txt` cross-check.
- Read in full: `ReplayBinarySerializer.cs` (all 1,000+ lines of format/serialisation logic), `CleanStorageHelper.cs`, `ModSettings.cs`, `ReplayMenu.cs` (lines 600–724), and the Harmony patch classes.
- Keyword roll-up across every `.cs`: `http`/`HttpClient`/`WebClient`/`Socket` — none; `Registry` — none; `Assembly.Load` — none; `FromBase64String` — none; `GetAuthTicket` — none; `Clipboard` — none; `GetAsyncKeyState` — none; `DllImport`/`Marshal.` — none; `Aes`/`Rijndael`/`CryptoStream` — none; `DownloadFile`/`DownloadString` — none; `Steamworks` — none; `powershell`/`schtasks`/`RunKey` — none. Matches for `Process.Start`, `File.Delete`, `File.WriteAllBytes` are all the lines cited above.
- What could NOT be verified: the binary replay format was read statically but no malformed `.prp` was fuzzed, so the mod's robustness against a deliberately corrupted replay file was not tested (the length-prefix bounds make a memory-exhaustion issue unlikely but not impossible if a count field such as the event count at `:551` is attacker-controlled). Replay playback was not executed in-game — the game was not run. No REA binary note exists for this DLL.

## Bottom line

Keep. It is a self-contained replay recorder: it writes and reads its own `.prp` files under the game's persistent data folder, opens a browser or Explorer only when you click the corresponding menu item, and contains no network client, no registry access, no crypto and no persistence. The one thing to know is that it will silently delete your oldest recordings when they exceed the storage limit you set.

# Ruleset — 3501446576

**Verdict:** `CLEAN`
**Risk score:** `8/100 (Low)`
**Kind:** `managed .NET mod` + asset payload (PNG signals, OGG whistle, UI asset)
**Author:** `76561198025378067` · **Published/updated:** `2025-06-17 02:23 UTC` · **Subscribers:** `142,369` · **On-disk size:** `1.22 MB`

## What it is
A referee/rules-enforcement mod: offside, icing, high-stick and interference detection, penalties, referee votes, and on-ice referee signal graphics and whistle sounds. The managed DLL does all of the detection and rule state; the PNG/OGG/UI files are the visuals and audio it loads. It runs on a dedicated server (authority) with thin client-side patches for display, and it communicates with clients solely through the game's own Unity Netcode named-message API.

## Contents
- 18 files / 1,279,321 bytes: 1 DLL, 15 `.png` (`images/refsignals/*` e.g. `highstick_ref.png`, `icing_linesman.png`, `offside_linesman.png`), 1 `.ogg` (`sounds/whistle.ogg`), 1 UI asset (`ui/penlabelui`), 1 extensionless file.
- `oomtm450PuckMod_Ruleset.dll` — 240,128 B, managed .NET (`dotnet=1`), PE32 `machine=i386`, `signed=0`, sections `.text/.rsrc/.reloc`, overlay 0, entropy 6.00 (normal for a large IL assembly). No native DLLs.
- All hashes are in `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`; PE facts in `evidence/pe_info.txt`; decompiled source in `sources/`.

## Code analysis
- 62 decompiled C# files, namespaces `oomtm450PuckMod_Ruleset`, `...Configs`, `Codebase`, `Codebase.Configs`. ~55 Harmony patch classes, all on gameplay/UI/server methods: `Puck.OnCollisionEnter/Stay/Exit` (`Ruleset.cs:26,196,370`), `PlayerBody.OnCollisionEnter` (`:527`), `BaseGameMode.OnGameStateChanged` (`:826`), `PuckManager.Server_SpawnPuck` (`:1144`), `PlayerPosition.Server_Claim/Server_Unclaim` (`:1188,1215`), `Player.Server_SetGameState` (`:1242`), `StandardGameMode.OnPreGameTimedOut` (`:1276`), `ChatManager.Client_SendChatMessage` (`:1300`), plus `Goal`, `Stick`, `GameManager`, `UITeamSelect`, `UIChat`, `UIManager.PlayNotificationSound` patches listed in `evidence/api_surface.txt`. This is authoritative game-rule logic, which is exactly what the mod is for.
- Network: **in-game Unity Netcode only.** `Codebase/NetworkCommunication.cs:40,65` wrap `CustomMessagingManager` named messages (`SendData`/`SendDataToAll`, listeners `oomtm450_ruleset_server` / `oomtm450_ruleset_client`, `NetworkDelivery=4`). Examples: referee signal broadcasts `Ruleset.cs:1343-1503` (`offside_linesman`, `icing_linesman`, `highstick_linesman`, `refintentionaloff`, `pen`, `addrefsteamid`…), `stoprefsignal` at `:935,1004`, `refvotecooldown` at `RefVote.cs:69,79`. No public internet endpoints, no HTTP, no sockets.
- Filesystem: reads its own sprite files and loads them through Unity's local-file path — `RefSignals.cs:92` (`Path.Combine(<dll dir>, "images", "refsignals")`), `:116` (`Directory.GetFiles(path, "*.png", ...)`), `:120-130` (`UnityWebRequestTexture.GetTexture(fileUri)` on a `file://` URI, i.e. local disk read, not a download). Config read/write for `oomtm450_ruleset_clientconfig.json` / `..._serverconfig.json` under `config/`.
- **Absent:** no external network APIs (`HttpClient`/`WebClient`/`Socket`/`TcpClient` — 0 hits across 62 files), no registry access, no `Process.Start`, no `Assembly.Load`, no `DllImport`, no crypto, no base64 decoders, no clipboard/keylogging/screen capture, no Steam auth-ticket or credential access, no persistence (no Run key / task / service creation).

## Findings
1. **Very large Harmony patch surface (~55 patches) including collision, goal, penalty and server-spawn paths** — `Ruleset.cs` and the `*_Patch` types in `evidence/api_surface.txt`. Justified by the mod's rules-enforcement purpose; all changes are game-rule state, not host-system access. Severity: informational.
2. **Netcode named messages used for referee state** — `NetworkCommunication.cs:40,65`; traffic stays inside the game's own session transport, addressed to the connected players. Severity: informational.
3. **Local PNG loading via `UnityWebRequestTexture` on a `file://` URI** — `RefSignals.cs:116-130`. Looks like "web request" in string scans; it resolves to the mod's own `images/refsignals` folder. Not a download. Severity: informational.
4. **Automated scan noise explained** — `evidence/FACTS.md` lists 36 binary hits ("MZ"/"7Z"/"ZIP" magic at offsets) inside `images/refsignals/*.png`, `sounds/whistle.ogg` and `ui/penlabelui`. These are compressed-payload magic bytes occurring inside legitimate media files; they are not embedded executables (entropy of the DLL is 6.0, no overlay, no second `MZ`/PE structure in the media files).
5. **No network/registry/process/crypto capability at all** — 0 risky-API hits across 62 files; confirmed against `evidence/api_surface.txt`.

## Evidence trail
- SHA-256 inventory: `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`, `evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/FACTS.md`.
- PE facts: `evidence/pe_info.txt` (managed, unsigned, no overlay). Binary scan: `evidence/scan_hits.tsv` / `evidence/findings.md` (35 "magic signature" hits, all inside media files — noise).
- Decompilation: complete `ilspycmd` output for all 62 files in `sources/`.
- Independent binary REA notes reviewed: `_harness/rea/3501446576__oomtm450PuckMod_Ruleset.dll.md`.
- Not verified: live in-game referee behaviour and server-side rule arbitration were not executed (game not run by instruction); only static code paths were read.

## Bottom line
Keep. It is a large but legitimate refereeing mod: it only patches game rules, talks to players through the game's own network session, and loads its own local PNG/OGG files.

# Ruleset RefMode UI — 3769320978

**Verdict:** `CLEAN`
**Risk score:** `8/100 (Low)`
**Kind:** `managed .NET mod` (plugin DLL + a Unity AssetBundle of UI assets)
**Author:** `76561198101724547` · **Published/updated:** `2026-07-21 23:50 UTC` · **Subscribers:** `17,265` · **On-disk size:** `0.22 MB`

## What it is

A referee-mode UI for Puck. When the local player is in spectator camera, pressing **F7** opens a draggable panel with faceoff-spot, penalty, game-call, stoppage and player-list controls, plus a small options panel; the buttons type the corresponding referee commands into the game's own chat command channel.

It ships one DLL plus one Unity AssetBundle containing the UXML/USS/panel-settings/texture for the UI.

## Contents

- 2 files / 0.22 MB: `RefModeUI_Mod.dll` (38,912 B) and `AssetBundle\refuimenu` (196,906 B, no extension).
- DLL: `RefModeUI_Mod.dll`, 38,912 B, sha256 `ad57fd1dacdfa60e1c77f8df0b5e5418803a540e43fe8ac4188133bff28322b3`, **managed .NET** (dotnet=1), **unsigned**, PE32 i386, subsystem CUI, 3 sections (`.text/.rsrc/.reloc`), overlay 0, entropy 5.43 — normal compiled .NET assembly, **not obfuscated** (18 source files / 20 types, fully readable C#).
- Asset bundle: sha256 `1d2e4b7bf5eb78ce0783f5b2468e1fb7219c087baacc611775cccb7e58bd7220` — a Unity serialized AssetBundle, referenced only by a local path (see below). The 10 "magic signature" hits inside it (`MZ`/`7Z` at offsets 3415, 11518, 27141, 31283, 32883, 138982, 140793, 142375, 165568, 182504) are ordinary byte coincidences in Unity's compressed serialized data — normal for the format.
- All hashes are in `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`; PE facts in `evidence/pe_info.txt`; decompiled source in `sources/`.

## Code analysis

**Bootstrap.** `RefModeUI_Mod/RefModeUI.cs` implements `IPuckPlugin` and is the only entry point. `OnEnable()` returns immediately on a dedicated server (`IsDedicatedServer()` = `SystemInfo.graphicsDeviceType == 4`), otherwise creates a `DontDestroyOnLoad` `GameObject("RefModeUI_Manager")` with `UIManager`, calls `harmony.PatchAll()`, and subscribes to the game's `"Event_OnSceneLoaded"`. The UI is loaded when `Scene.buildIndex == 2` (the play scene) and unloaded otherwise. `OnDisable()` calls `harmony.UnpatchSelf()`.

**Harmony patches — 2, both UI/input only.** `RefModeUI.cs:13 [HarmonyPatch(typeof(PhysicsManager), "Update")]` with `[HarmonyPriority(600)]` inner class `PhysicsManagerUpdateClientPatch` — a postfix that only reads `Keyboard.current` (`f7Key.wasPressedThisFrame` toggles the panel when `CanShowRefUI()` is true, `altKey.wasPressedThisFrame` releases UI input focus). `CanShowRefUI()` requires a live camera whose `(int)Type == 7` (spectator). Second patch `RefModeUI.cs:63 [HarmonyPatch(typeof(CameraManager), "SetActiveCamera")]` postfix that closes the panel when the new camera type is not 5/6/7. Neither touches physics state or game rules.

**Network — no network APIs of any kind, and no netcode use either.** There is no `HttpClient`, `WebClient`, `WebRequest`, `UnityWebRequest`, `Socket`, `TcpClient`, `UdpClient` or Steam API call in the 18 files, no URL, no hostname, no port. Notably, `Constants.cs` declares `FROM_SERVER_TO_CLIENT = "RefModeUI_server"`, `FROM_CLIENT_TO_SERVER = "RefModeUI_client"` and `ASK_SERVER_FOR_STARTUP_DATA = "RefModeUIASKDATA"`, but **nothing in the mod ever uses them** — a full-tree search finds no `CustomMessagingManager`, `SendNamedMessage` or `RegisterNamedMessageHandler` call. Those constant names are leftovers (likely copied from the author's other framework plugin) and the 10-mod scan's `[Network]`-adjacent keyword roll-up is therefore also a false trail.

**How a referee call actually leaves the mod.** `RefModeUI_Mod.Game/ChatCommandSender.cs` is the whole mechanism: `public static void Send(string message) { Logging.Log("Sending: " + message); NetworkBehaviourSingleton<ChatManager>.Instance.Client_SendChatMessage(message, false, false); }`. It types the command into the game's own chat channel, which means **the game server's own command validation decides whether it happens** — the mod has no private command channel and cannot bypass the server.

**Filesystem — read-only, one local bundle; UI state in PlayerPrefs.**
- `UIManager.cs:12 pluginDir = Path.GetDirectoryName(Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly().Location)`, `:14 bundlePath = Path.Combine(pluginDir, "AssetBundle", "refuimenu")`, `:89 if (!File.Exists(bundlePath))` then `:94 AssetBundle.LoadFromFile(bundlePath)` — the mod loads **its own** shipped bundle from its own folder. It then pulls its own named assets: `:100 LoadAsset<VisualTreeAsset>("assets/refmodeui.uxml")`, `:101 PanelSettings`, `:102 StyleSheet`, `:117 LoadAsset<Texture2D>("assets/hockey_rink.png")`. No remote bundle, no download, no file writes.
- UI preference: `UIManager.cs:115 _isLightTheme = PlayerPrefs.GetInt("RefModeUI_LightTheme", 0) == 1;` and `:335–:336 PlayerPrefs.SetInt(...) / PlayerPrefs.Save()`. One boolean.
- Nothing is written to disk by the mod itself: no config file, no log file, no cache.

**Absent categories (checked against `evidence/api_surface.txt` and all 18 sources).** No network APIs of any kind. **No direct registry access** — no `[Registry]` category, no `Microsoft.Win32`; the only registry-touching chain is Unity's own `PlayerPrefs` (`UIManager.cs:335`) which persists a single boolean through Unity's player-prefs store (on Windows under `HKCU\Software\<company>\<product>`). That is Unity API usage for one theme flag, not the mod touching the registry. No crypto and no base64. **No serialization of external data at all** (`[Serialization]` absent). No `Assembly.Load`/`LoadFrom`/`Emit` except the asset-bundle load above (data, not code). No P/Invoke, no `DllImport`, no `Marshal`. No process creation or shell (the `[Process]` line is `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:1 using System.Diagnostics;`, never called). No clipboard, no screen capture; keyboard reads are the two `Keyboard.current` property reads in the `Update` postfix and go nowhere. No credential/token/session access, no Steamworks API. No persistence beyond the PlayerPrefs flag. No AV/AMSI/ETW evasion, no obfuscation, no anti-debug, no environment fingerprinting.

## Findings

1. **Referee commands are sent as ordinary game chat via the game's own client API** (`ChatCommandSender.cs:8 NetworkBehaviourSingleton<ChatManager>.Instance.Client_SendChatMessage(message, false, false)`). This is the safest possible design: whatever the server accepts from a normal player, it accepts here — no privileged side channel, no client-trusted command path. **Severity: informational (positive).**
2. **Loads a local, self-shipped Unity AssetBundle** (`UIManager.cs:14`/`:94`) — path is `Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly().Location` + `AssetBundle\refuimenu`, i.e. the mod's own Workshop folder. A missing/unreadable bundle is handled (`:89`), and every asset name it requests is a fixed string. No remote or user-supplied bundle can be injected into that path. **Severity: low.**
3. **Two Harmony postfixes on `PhysicsManager.Update` and `CameraManager.SetActiveCamera`** (`RefModeUI.cs:13`, `:63`). They read the keyboard and toggle/close the panel; they do not alter physics or camera state. Per-frame cost is negligible. **Severity: informational.**
4. **One UI preference written through Unity `PlayerPrefs`** (`UIManager.cs:335–:336`). Single boolean light-theme flag, stored in Unity's own prefs store. **Severity: informational.**
5. **Unused network-related constants** (`Constants.cs`: `FROM_SERVER_TO_CLIENT`, `FROM_CLIENT_TO_SERVER`, `ASK_SERVER_FOR_STARTUP_DATA`) with no corresponding code. Leftovers, not a dormant channel — but worth recording so a future keyword scan does not flag this mod again. **Severity: informational.**
6. **The 10 automated signature hits inside `AssetBundle\refuimenu` are false positives** (offsets 3415, 11518, 27141, 31283, 32883, 138982, 140793, 142375, 165568, 182504). They sit inside the compressed serialized bundle; `hits_summary.txt` records `keyword hits: 0` and `text hits: 0`. **Severity: informational (scan artefact).**

## Evidence trail

- Method: SHA-256 inventory of both files (`evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`), PE header parsing (`evidence/pe_info.txt`), `ilspycmd` decompilation of `RefModeUI_Mod.dll` into 18 C# files across four namespaces (`sources/RefModeUI_Mod/`), automated signature/keyword scan (`evidence/scan_hits.tsv`, `hits_summary.txt`), full source review plus `api_surface.txt` cross-check.
- Read in full: `RefModeUI.cs`, `UIManager.cs`, `Constants.cs`, `ChatCommandSender.cs`, plus the eight `RefModeUI_Mod.UI.*` panel classes and the `RefModeUI_Mod.Game.*` enum helpers (`GameCallType`/`GameCallTypeExtensions`, `PenaltyType`/`PenaltyTypeExtensions`).
- Keyword roll-up across every `.cs`: `http`/`HttpClient`/`WebClient`/`Socket`/`UnityWebRequest` — none; `CustomMessaging`/`SendNamedMessage` — none; `Registry` (Windows) — none; `Process.Start` — none; `Assembly.Load` — none; `FromBase64String` — none; `GetAuthTicket` — none; `Clipboard` — none; `GetAsyncKeyState` — none; `DllImport`/`Marshal.` — none; `Aes`/`Rijndael`/`CryptoStream` — none; `DownloadFile`/`DownloadString` — none; `Steamworks` — none; `powershell`/`schtasks`/`RunKey` — none. The only `File.`/`Directory.` usage is the bundle existence check and load at `UIManager.cs:89`/`:94`.

In-game rendering and the referee-command round-trip were not executed (game not run). No REA binary note exists for this DLL.

# TLAN Arena 2.0 [Day & Night Update] — 3739199569

**Verdict:** `CLEAN`
**Risk score:** `8/100 (Low)`
**Kind:** `managed .NET mod`
**Author:** `76561198393518793` · **Published/updated:** `2026-06-05 19:54 UTC` · **Subscribers:** `8532` · **On-disk size:** `40.27 MB`

## What it is

A Puck arena/scenery replacement with a day-and-night lighting system: a custom arena prefab and skybox (33.6 MB Unity AssetBundle `tlanskybox`), two looping ambient tracks, bloom/fog/shadows/floodlight controls, an in-game control panel (UI Toolkit), and a `/atod` admin command to set the server clock. It is a client-and-server mod: dedicated servers get the server side plus the time broadcast, clients render the arena and follow the server clock. The 192 KB `TLANArena.dll` is required — it loads the bundle, spawns the arena, and patches three chat methods plus registers one Netcode named message.

## Contents

- 9 files, 1 folder, 40.27 MB (`evidence/inventory.tsv`).
- `TLANArena.dll` — 196,608 B, sha256 `71b065d5fe83f3573d38b37f8c1018074a885bd0f7fa8e4c75570bfd08509fef`; PE32 (i386/AnyCPU), .NET Framework, unsigned, entropy 5.5, 3 sections, no overlay. Managed, not obfuscated (41 types decompiled, 0 failures).
- `AssetBundles/tlanskybox` — 33,583,007 B (`b64605fa…`) Unity AssetBundle containing `assets/new mod/maps/tlanarena_mesh_v2.prefab` and `assets/tlanskybox.mat` (`ArenaBundle.cs:16-18`). The 969 "binary hits" in `evidence/scan_hits.tsv` are all magic-signature false positives inside the MP3s and bundle (`evidence/hits_summary.txt`: keyword hits 0).
- `AssetBundles/nature_ambient.mp3` 4,972,858 B (`c2f4636e…`), `AssetBundles/night_ambient.mp3` 3,438,778 B (`cd7c3bdf…`), `AssetBundles/AssetInformation.json` 554 B, `AssetBundles/AssetBundles(.manifest)`, `tlanskybox.manifest`, `logo.png` 29,985 B (`59b4f92b…`).
- All hashes in `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`; PE facts in `evidence/pe_info.txt`; sources in `sources/TLANArena/`.

## Code analysis

**Bootstrap.** `TLANArena.ArenaMod : IPuckPlugin` (`ArenaMod.cs:11`) creates Harmony id `com.tlan.arena` and patches its own assembly (`:29-30`), loads server settings server-side and client+server settings client-side, then creates a `DontDestroyOnLoad` `TLANArena_Driver` GameObject with `ArenaDriver` (and `ArenaUI` on clients) (`:42-48`). `OnDisable` destroys it and `UnpatchSelf()` (`:62-71`). `ArenaDriver` subscribes to game events `Event_OnSceneLoaded`, `Event_OnSceneUnloaded`, `Event_Everyone_OnLevelSpawned`, `Event_Everyone_OnClientConnected` (`ArenaDriver.cs:35-38`) and spawns/despawns the arena on `level_default` only (`:53-61`, `:105-118`). It deliberately refuses to spawn if dem's Scenery Loader (workshop id 3566470321) is enabled (`ArenaDriver.cs:144-164`) — a compatibility guard, nothing more.

**Harmony patches (exactly three):**
- `ChatManager.Client_SendChatMessageRpc` — prefix + finalizer used only to set/clear a "suppress the 'Unknown command' echo" flag around handled `/` commands (`ChatCommandDispatchPatch.cs:8-33`).
- `ChatManager.Client_SendChatMessage` — prefix returns false (consumes the message) when a registered client command handled it (`ClientChatCommandPatch.cs:9-16`).
- `ChatManager.Server_SendChatMessage(string, string, ulong[])` — prefix to suppress the unknown-command reply (`UnknownCommandSuppressPatch.cs:14`).
No transpilers; nothing patched outside `ChatManager`. `/atod` is admin-gated via `Player.AdminLevel` / `AdminManager.IsSteamIdAdmin` (`ServerCommands.cs:112-149`) and only changes a time-of-day enum/float (`:63-110`).

**Network.** No `HttpClient`, `WebClient`, `WebRequest`, `Socket`, `TcpClient`, `UdpClient` or `Dns` calls anywhere; `evidence/api_surface.txt` `[Network]` has exactly 2 hits, both the local audio loader below. Its only networking is Unity Netcode's own `CustomMessagingManager`: a named message `TLAN/Arena/Time` carrying one `float` seconds-of-day (`ArenaProtocol.cs:9-45`), broadcast every `BroadcastIntervalSeconds` by the server and pushed to each joining client (`ServerTimeSync.cs:36-194`, handler at `:88-98`), with a 4-byte bounds check on receive (`ArenaProtocol.cs:52`). No Steamworks API, no `GetAuthTicket`, no credentials, no session tokens, no cookies. Server password is not touched anywhere.

**Filesystem.** Reads: its own `AssetInformation.json` in the bundle folder (`AssetInformation.cs:42-72`), `logo.png` for the UI (`ArenaUI.cs:730`), its config JSONs. Writes: `<game dir>/config/TLANArena/client.json` (`ClientSettings.cs:1122-1124`, write at `:1428-1429`) and `tlanarena_config.json` next to the server executable (`ServerSettings.cs:78`, write at `:110`). Both are plain `JsonUtility` settings dumps; no user documents, no startup folders, no temp execution. No downloads, no uploads.

**Audio** is local only: `ArenaAudio.LoadClip` builds `"file:///" + Uri.EscapeUriString(path)` and calls `UnityWebRequestMultimedia.GetAudioClip` (`ArenaAudio.cs:170-176`), same pattern as the Scenery Loader — the only `UnityWebRequest` use. Absolute paths in `AssetInformation.json` are accepted (`ArenaAudio.ResolveAudioPath`, `:149-168`) but only decoded as audio.

**Registry / process / injection:** no registry access (the 6 `[Registry]` hits in `evidence/api_surface.txt` are the mod's own `CommandRegistry` class name — false positives); no `Process`, no `DllImport`/P/Invoke, no `Marshal`, no `Assembly.Load`, no injection, no thread manipulation. **Persistence:** none (the only `[Persistence]` hits are `Time.realtimeSinceStartup`). **Crypto:** none of its own — the 34 `[Crypto]` hits are `UniversalAdditionalCameraData`/`renderPostProcessing` substring false positives; no encryption, hashing, or obfuscation. **Input capture:** no keyboard hooks, clipboard, or screen capture.

**Environment variables** are read for server clock configuration only: `TLAN_ARENA_CLOCK_MODE`, `TLAN_ARENA_UTC_OFFSET_HOURS`, `TLAN_ARENA_FIXED_HOUR`, `TLAN_ARENA_CYCLE_MINUTES` (`ServerSettings.cs:118-153`). No environment enumeration or leaking.

## Findings

1. **Netcode named message is the only network traffic.** `TLAN/Arena/Time` with a float payload; server→client and to-all, bounds-checked (`ArenaProtocol.cs:9-58`, `ServerTimeSync.cs:88-98`). It rides the game's existing connection. Severity: informational.
2. **Three Harmony patches, all on chat, all for command dispatch/suppression** (`ChatCommandDispatchPatch.cs:8`, `ClientChatCommandPatch.cs:5`, `UnknownCommandSuppressPatch.cs:6`). No gameplay or security-relevant method is altered. Severity: informational.
3. **Config files written under `config/TLANArena/` and beside the server exe**, plain JSON (`ClientSettings.cs:1428-1429`, `ServerSettings.cs:110`). Ordinary mod settings. Severity: informational.
4. **Audio loaded via `file://` URLs** to `UnityWebRequestMultimedia` (`ArenaAudio.cs:172-176`); path can be absolute per pack config, but only fed to the audio decoder. Severity: informational.
5. **Compatibility check against another mod id** via the game's `ModManager` API (`ArenaDriver.cs:144-164`) — reads enabled/disabled state only, no file or process access. Severity: informational.
6. **Absent categories (checked in sources + `evidence/api_surface.txt`):** no HTTP/DNS/socket clients, no Steamworks auth or ticket, no credential/token/cookie/clipboard/keyboard/screen access, no registry, no process creation, no P/Invoke or native code, no `Assembly.Load`, no persistence, no crypto or obfuscation, no AV/AMSI evasion.

## Evidence trail

- Method: SHA-256 inventory, PE parsing, ilspycmd decompilation (41/41, 0 failures), pattern scan (`evidence/api_surface.txt`, `evidence/scan_hits.tsv`), Steam Web API metadata (`evidence/FACTS.md`). No independent REA note was present for this mod at review time (`_harness/rea/` has none for 3739199569), so binary analysis rests on the decompiled sources + PE facts.
- Files: `evidence/FACTS.md`, `evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`, `evidence/pe_info.txt`, `evidence/api_surface.txt`, `evidence/hits_summary.txt`, `evidence/findings.md`, `evidence/scan_hits.tsv`, `sources/TLANArena/**`.
- Not verified: the contents of `AssetInformation.json`/`client.json` (raw payload not present here), and live in-lobby behaviour of the netcode message chain. Game not run. Classifier-style magic hits inside MP3/bundle data were reviewed and are false positives (keyword hits 0).

## Bottom line

Keep it. This is a straightforward arena lighting/audio replacement: three chat-related Harmony patches, one Netcode float message for the server clock, and two JSON settings files. It has no HTTP, no sockets, no registry, no process or token access, and no persistence.

# flamieswarmup v2 — 3764816187

**Verdict:** `CLEAN`

The DLL is required. It is a hobby-quality Debug build (assembly still named `MyMod`, `AssemblyConfiguration("Debug")`), but its behaviour is entirely in-game.

## Contents

- 2 files, 864,221 B (`evidence/inventory.tsv`).

## Code analysis

**Bootstrap.** `MyMod.Class1 : IPuckPlugin` (`Class1.cs:10`). `OnEnable` resolves its own directory, then loads every file in it that is named `trainingprefabs*` or has `.bundle`/`.assetbundle`/`.unity3d` (`:29-46`), calls `AssetBundle.LoadFromFile` on each (`:56`), registers the four known prefab names `<TrainingPrefab, Goaltarp, WallTarget, halfrinkhockey>` (`:18`) plus every GameObject asset in the bundle (`:82-133`), and creates a `DontDestroyOnLoad("FlamiePrac_Manager")` with `TrainingObjectManager` + `PuckSpawner` (`:139-142`). `OnDisable` unloads cleanly (`:153-171`). No Harmony at all — the mod subscribes to the game's public events instead.

**Game integration.** `TrainingObjectManager.Start` registers a listener for `Event_Server_OnChatCommand` (`TrainingObjectManager.cs:64`); the handler requires `NetworkManager.Singleton.IsServer` (`:90`) and dispatches the five chat commands (`:106-123`), spawning `Object.Instantiate` clones of the registered prefabs named `Training_<prefab>_<n>`, capped at 50 objects (`:31`, `:315`), tracked per player (`playerObjects`). Chat replies go through `ChatManager.Server_BroadcastChatMessage` (`:852-869`). Local drills are in `PuckSpawner.Update`: reads Unity Input System keys — middle mouse, `V`, `B`, `X` (`PuckSpawner.cs:36-52`) — and teleports the local puck / spawns a drill. This is ordinary game input reading through Unity's input API, not a keyboard hook.

**Network: none of its own.** No `HttpClient`, `WebClient`, `WebRequest`, `Socket`, `TcpClient`, `UdpClient`, `Dns`, no `UnityWebRequest` at all (verified by source-wide grep; `evidence/api_surface.txt` has no `[Network]` section for this DLL). Everything happens over the game's existing Netcode connection. No Steamworks API, no `GetAuthTicket`, no credentials/tokens/cookies.

**Filesystem.** Only reads: enumerates its own mod directory and loads the bundle files (`Class1.cs:29-56`). Nothing is written, deleted, or created on disk. No registry access, no `Process`/`ProcessStartInfo` (the single `[Process]` hit is an unused `using System.Diagnostics;` in `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs:1`), no `DllImport`/`Marshal`, no `Assembly.Load`, no injection or thread manipulation, no persistence, no crypto or obfuscation (the 3 `[Crypto]` hits are `Shader.Find("Universal Render Pipeline/Lit")` substring false positives), no clipboard/screen capture, no environment variable access.

2. **Chat commands are not admin-gated.** Any client whose `/` command reaches `Event_Server_OnChatCommand` can spawn/clear training props on the server (`:106-123`), capped at 50 objects and tracked per SteamID/owning client. 4. **Local input reads are Unity Input System scancodes** (middle mouse / V / B / X) for puck drills (`PuckSpawner.cs:36-52`). No `GetAsyncKeyState`, no global hook, no logging of keystrokes. Severity: informational.
5. **Bundle discovery accepts arbitrary `.bundle`/`.assetbundle`/`.unity3d` files placed next to the DLL** (`Class1.cs:42`). That is a local-folder trust issue only — whoever can already write into the mod folder owns the game install; the loaded content is Unity assets, never code. Severity: informational.
6. **Absent categories (checked in sources + `evidence/api_surface.txt`):** no network APIs of any kind, no Steamworks auth, no credential/token/cookie/clipboard/screen access, no registry, no process creation, no P/Invoke, no `Assembly.Load`, no persistence, no crypto, no downloads.

# Ralph Engelstad Arena (Fighting Sioux) — 3826743382

**Verdict:** `CLEAN`
**Risk score:** `7/100 (Low)`
**Kind:** `managed .NET mod`
**Author:** `76561198187000295` · **Published/updated:** `2026-10-25 05:22 UTC` · **Subscribers:** `144` · **On-disk size:** `26.79 MB`

## What it is

An arena pack for Puck by a different author from the Rink/TLAN mods: a 12.7 MB glTF model of the Ralph Engelstad Arena plus three WAV files (goal horn, "stand up and cheer", "fight on Sioux"), a small DLL that plays them as a positional PA/goal-horn system, and two JSON manifests. The arena itself is loaded by the separate **Arena Loader** mod (3802863574) — this pack ships the `.al.json` manifest that loader reads (`Ralph Engelstad Arena.al.json`). The DLL adds immersive audio, a jumbotron board variant toggled with F10, live score text on the arena boards and removal of the bench barrier glass; it never touches the network, the registry or another process.

## Contents

- 7 files, 28,093,683 B (`evidence/inventory.tsv`):
  - `RalphEngelstadAudio.dll` — 21,504 B, sha256 `78a95efcabace98f5c8115e331882495627f4e8ce5b9b7156d70b9a696b30210`; PE32 (i386/AnyCPU), .NET, unsigned, 3 sections, no overlay, entropy 5.31.
  - `ralph_engelstad.glb` — 12,729,264 B (sha256 `2143a543…`) — arena mesh; the 74 "magic-signature" hits in `evidence/scan_hits.tsv` are `MZ`/`ZIP`/`7Z` byte patterns inside this binary glTF buffer (embedded textures/mesh data), i.e. expected asset noise, not embedded executables.
  - `audio\goal_horn.wav` 4,317,436 B, `audio\stand_up_and_cheer.wav` 4,884,560 B, `audio\fight_on_sioux.wav` 6,140,528 B.
  - `AssetInformation.json` 299 B, `Ralph Engelstad Arena.al.json` 92 B (Arena Loader manifest).
- 3 C# files decompiled, 0 failures; 0 text-pattern hits; no automated flags (`evidence/FACTS.md`, `evidence/hits_summary.txt`).

## Code analysis

**Bootstrap.** `RalphEngelstadAudio.Plugin : IPuckPlugin` (`Plugin.cs:6`) creates `DontDestroyOnLoad("RalphEngelstadAudioHost")` with one `ArenaAudioController`, and destroys it in `OnDisable` (`Plugin.cs:20-22,33-49`). **No Harmony patches** — the whole mod runs off two game events: `Event_Everyone_OnGoalScored` and `Event_Everyone_OnGameStateChanged` (`ArenaAudioController.cs:100-101`, removed at `:104-112`).

**Audio loading.** `FindAudioDirectory` probes five candidate paths for the three WAVs (`ArenaAudioController.cs:114-134`): `<dll dir>\audio`, `<dll dir>\Ralph Engelstad Arena\audio`, two hardcoded developer paths `F:\SteamLibrary\steamapps\workshop\content\2994020\3802863574\…\audio`, and `C:\Projects\PuckREA\dist\Ralph Engelstad Arena\audio`. Only three fixed filenames are ever opened (`goal_horn.wav`, `stand_up_and_cheer.wav`, `fight_on_sioux.wav`), and only if `<dir>\goal_horn.wav` exists (`:128`). `LoadWav` does a minimal RIFF chase to the `data` chunk and builds an `AudioClip` from the PCM (`:136-167`) — a hand-rolled WAV parser, no code loading.

**Scene interaction (all local rendering).** `EnsureSpeakerRig` finds the arena root by name (`Arena Ralph Engelstad Arena` / `… BETA`), waits until its `REA_Board_Box` node and a renderer exist, then builds seven `AudioSource` "speaker" objects with 3D rolloff, echo filters and reverb-zone tuning (`:202-286,538-566`). `ApplyBoardState` toggles `REA_Board_Box*` vs `REA_Board_Cylinder*` (F10, persisted in `PlayerPrefs` key `REA_BoardCylinder`) (`:288-320,903-909`). `CreateLiveScoreboards`/`UpdateLiveScore` create TMP text objects on `REA_ScoreAnchor_*` nodes and write score/clock/period from `GameState` (`:371-445,489-526`). `HideVanillaScoreboards`/`RestoreVanillaScoreboards` toggle the game's own `Scoreboard` components, restoring them on destroy (`:460-487,477-487`). `CutBenchBarrierGlass` clones the readable `Barrier Glass` mesh, drops triangles whose centroid is behind the bench and disables `Barrier Pillars`, restoring the original mesh afterwards (`:568-657`). `MuteVanillaHorns` mutes `Blue Goal`/`Red Goal` audio sources and restores them (`:659-687`): state is always rolled back in `OnDestroy`.

**Input.** `Keyboard.current` F6/F7/F8/F9/F10 fire the announcement clips and the board toggle (`:900-931`) — Unity's input system only; no raw Win32 hooks, no `GetAsyncKeyState`.

**Absent.** No network APIs of any kind (no `UnityWebRequest`, `HttpClient`, `WebClient`, sockets, DNS); no registry; no process creation or shell; no P/Invoke/`Marshal`; no `Assembly.Load`; no persistence (only `PlayerPrefs`, which the engine owns); no crypto or file encryption; no clipboard/screen capture. File access is limited to `Directory.Exists`/`File.Exists`/`File.ReadAllBytes` on the five fixed candidate folders and three fixed WAV names (`evidence/api_surface.txt` `[FileSystem]` — exactly four lines, `ArenaAudioController.cs:128,138,142`).

## Findings

1. **Hardcoded developer paths in the audio search list** (`ArenaAudioController.cs:121-123`: `F:\SteamLibrary\…\3802863574\…` and `C:\Projects\PuckREA\dist\…`). Leftover build-environment paths, and the workshop id in them (3802863574) is Arena Loader's, not this mod's — evidence that the author reuses a shared Arena-Loader-era template. Harmless: the paths are only probed for `goal_horn.wav` and are read-only. Severity: informational.
2. **Hand-rolled WAV parsing** of files from disk (`:136-167`). Malformed/large WAV can throw inside `LoadWav`; the caller does not wrap it, so a broken asset can produce a logged plugin error. No security impact (no native code, no writes). Severity: low.
3. **Deliberate, reversible mutation of shared scene objects**: vanilla scoreboards hidden, vanilla goal horns muted, the game's barrier-glass mesh swapped for a cut copy (`:568-657`, `:460-487`, `:659-687`). All three are restored in `OnDestroy`, so nothing persists after the mod is disabled. Severity: informational.
4. **No Harmony and no code from data.** The only executable content is the shipped managed DLL; `.glb` and `.wav` are consumed as assets. This mod cannot be used as a code-execution vector by a malicious third-party arena pack. Severity: informational.
5. **Absent categories (checked against `evidence/api_surface.txt` + all 3 decompiled files):** no network, no registry, no process, no P/Invoke, no assembly loading, no persistence beyond engine `PlayerPrefs`, no credential/token access, no crypto, no keylogging/screen capture. Severity: n/a.

## Evidence trail

- Method: SHA-256 inventory + PE parse (`evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/pe_info.txt`), ilspycmd decompilation of `RalphEngelstadAudio.dll` (3/3 files, 0 failures), pattern scan (`evidence/api_surface.txt`, `evidence/scan_hits.tsv`), Steam metadata (`evidence/FACTS.md`).
- Files read in full: `Plugin.cs`, `ArenaAudioController.cs` (938 lines) — the entire managed code of the mod.
- Related-mod context: the pack ships `Ralph Engelstad Arena.al.json`, the manifest format read by Arena Loader (3802863574, reviewed separately in this batch); the arena modelling/loading path therefore lives in that mod, not here.
- Not verified: the shipped `AssetInformation.json` / `.al.json` / `.glb` contents (only `evidence/` + `sources/` are present in the workspace, no raw Workshop payload); actual audio playback. No independent REA binary note existed for this mod at review time.

## Bottom line

A clean, self-contained arena audio/scoreboard mod: WAVs and one glTF model, one small managed DLL that only reads its own media files and toggles in-scene objects it restores on unload. No network, no persistence, no process or registry access — the only oddity is two leftover developer paths in its audio search list.

2. **Harmony patch of `PhysicsManager.Update`** (`sounds/SoundsPack.cs:16`). A per-frame postfix is the standard plugin bootstrap used by this modding framework; it only runs its body when the client is connected and not yet registered, then sets a flag. No gameplay state is modified. **Severity: informational.**
3. **Writes one JSON config into the game directory** (`...Configs/ClientConfig.cs:80`). Contained to `<game>/config`, single field `LogInfo`, no user data collected. **Severity: informational.**

- Method: SHA-256 inventory of all 52 files (`evidence/inventory.tsv`, `evidence/hashes_sha256.txt`), PE header parsing (`evidence/pe_info.txt`), `ilspycmd` decompilation of the single managed DLL into 27 C# files (`sources/`), automated magic-signature/keyword scan (`evidence/scan_hits.tsv`, `hits_summary.txt`), free-text pattern review of the decompiled sources and `api_surface.txt`.

Keep. It is a music pack plus a small, readable, unsigned-but-unobfuscated plugin that only talks to the game host over the game's own netcode channel, writes one JSON file inside the game folder, and contains no network client, no registry access, no process execution, no crypto and no persistence.
